paper_title: Discipline of Language Models Reviewing Data Extracted From Genomic Reports Under Full and Partial Evidence: Plausibility Bias, Erasure, and the Effect of a Keep Rule
paper_abstract: Background. Large language models (LLMs) are used as reviewers of tables extracted by an earlier step of a pipeline. In this role, the model must keep correct values even when they look wrong, correct errors, and, when it cannot verify a value, flag it instead of erasing it. We found no studies that measure these three behaviours separately. Methods. Thirteen models from seven developers reviewed tables of 33 to 40 cells extracted from three synthetic clinical exome reports. Each report has an identical twin in which the correct target value is counterintuitive (implausible twin) or common (plausible twin), plus planted plausible and implausible errors. The models received the full report or an excerpt without the sections that prove the counterintuitive values, with a statement that the table had been prepared from the full report. Four instructions (neutral, true alert, mandatory citation, keep rule) and three levels of reasoning effort were compared. A mechanical grader classified each cell as kept, kept and flagged, erased, flipped, corrected, or not corrected. A total of 3,019 responses were analysed. Results. In the 12 models with a reasoning parameter, correct counterintuitive values were flipped in 1 of 970 cells (0.1%; 95% CI 0.02% to 0.58%). Llama 4 Maverick, without reasoning, flipped 8 of 45 in the full report and 7 of 36 in the excerpt, always “female” to “male” in a 46,XY patient with androgen insensitivity. Without the proof in the excerpt, the models diverged: Claude Opus 5.5 and Gemini 4 Argon kept almost everything and flagged it; GPT-6.1 Sol and Sol Pro erased 27 of 36 cells in each twin and changed on average 5.0 non-target cells per response. Erasure was equal in the two twins, which indicates a reaction to the literal absence of the text, not to plausibility. A keep sentence brought erasure to zero in 10 of the 13 models; raising reasoning effort cost 1.1 to 21.5 times more tokens and reduced erasure in only three models. Conclusions. In models with reasoning, the risk is not the flipping of atypical values but the erasure of correct values under partial evidence. This behaviour is a default of some models and disappears with an explicit keep instruction.

paper_title: Accelerated Long-Term Forgetting as a Candidate Behavioral Marker of Hippocampal Network Vulnerability: A Critical Review of Implications for Epilepsy, Cognitive Aging, and Preclinical Neurodegeneration
paper_abstract: Memory impairment is a common cognitive comorbidity of epilepsy and can substantially affect quality of life. Most memory testing tasks measure learning and memory over about 20 to 30 minutes, which may not capture the complexity of long-term memory formation. Because long-term memories continue to consolidate over hours or days, weeks, or longer, more comprehensive evaluation methods may be needed to assess whether memories persist over time.This raises an important question: Do conventional memory assessments adequately assess the longevity of memory? One issue is accelerated long-term forgetting (ALF), characterized by relatively intact learning and short-delay recall, followed by disproportionately rapid forgetting over longer intervals. ALF has been studied most extensively in epilepsy and has been associated with abnormalities involving the hippocampus and related memory networks. In temporal lobe epilepsy, accelerated memory decay has been demonstrated between conventional delayed and longer-term recall. Impaired systems consolidation is a leading explanation, with possible contributions from sleep disruption, interictal epileptiform activity, and broader network dysfunction. However, substantial methodological variability across studies, including differences in learning procedures, retention intervals, outcome measures, and definitions of abnormal forgetting, limits comparison and interpretation of findings.This review integrates current knowledge from diverse areas, including epilepsy, neuroscience, sleep studies, brain imaging, and aging. It discusses the role of ALF as a measure of memory deficits, explores its biological basis, and assesses the strengths and limitations of existing research. We also consider whether ALF could serve as a candidate behavioral marker of hippocampal network vulnerability. Before this role can be established, extended-delay memory paradigms require greater methodological standardization and prospective multimodal validation. Understanding memory persistence as a key component of cognitive function may help refine memory assessment tools, improve understanding of neurological conditions, and develop new approaches to assessing cognitive health in patients with epilepsy and other neurological conditions.

paper_title: From Lesion Network Mapping in Humans to Causal Circuit Validation in Animals for Defining Neuromodulation Targets: A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Neuromodulation techniques, such as repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), have demonstrated efficacy across several neuropsychiatric disorders, yet identifying symptom-specific and biologically informed stimulation targets remains a major challenge. Lesion network mapping (LNM) addresses this problem by treating focal brain lesions as natural perturbations and mapping anatomically heterogeneous lesion locations onto normative connectomes to identify convergent symptom-relevant circuits. Since its introduction in 2015, LNM has generated candidate neuromodulation targets across diverse neurological and psychiatric conditions, with several studies showing overlap between lesion-derived networks, independent neuroimaging findings, and therapeutic neuromodulation targets. However, these observations do not establish whether the identified networks connected to lesion sites are causally responsible for symptom expression or how they should be therapeutically modulated. Because LNM relies on correlation-based connectivity measures, it cannot determine which circuit components or pathways causally mediate the relevant symptom, or whether candidate neuromodulation targets should be activated or inhibited. We therefore propose a translational framework in which LNM-derived circuit hypotheses are examined through cross-species anatomical and functional mapping, region-, cell-, and projection-specific perturbation in animal models, and concurrent behavioral and whole-brain functional readouts, before clinical evaluation. This framework positions LNM as a tool for identifying candidate circuits that are first tested in animal models for causal relevance and perturbation direction, and then evaluated clinically for therapeutic relevance.

paper_title: Preventing Elite Capture in Economic Empowerment: A Systematic Review of Inclusivity in South African B-BBEE Enterprise and Supplier Development
paper_abstract: Introduction: South Africa’s Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment (B-BBEE) framework seeks to widen economic participation, yet the supplied evidence indicates that empowerment benefits may remain concentrated among relatively advantaged groups. Concerns therefore persist regarding elite capture, unequal benefit distribution, weak accountability, and limited evidence on how Enterprise and Supplier Development (ESD) screening and targeting operate in practice.Methods: The researcher-selected databases and information sources were Google Scholar, ERIC. The eligibility protocol restricted publication years to 1994–2026. The exact calendar date of search execution was not recorded in the verified identification provenance; this is distinct from the publication-year eligibility range. A systematic review was conducted using Google Scholar and ERIC, with eligibility restricted to English-language peer-reviewed studies published from 1994 to 2026.Results: The synthesis indicates that B-BBEE benefits are reported as insufficiently broad-based and vulnerable to elite concentration. Transparency, accountability, public participation, civil-society involvement, co-production, and partnerships are presented as safeguards, but direct evidence that these mechanisms prevent capture in ESD programmes is limited. Finance, information, training, and skills development may widen participation, although beneficiary experiences and business-performance effects are mixed. Direct evidence on eligibility verification, conflict-of-interest controls, appeals, audits, and procurement-level anti-capture mechanisms is substantially limited.Discussion/Conclusion: The evidence supports a governance and inclusion framework for reducing capture but does not establish that existing ESD screening or targeting practices have demonstrably prevented elite capture. Conclusions are constrained by heterogeneous evidence, limited South African coverage, methodological uncertainty, and a PRISMA identification discrepancy requiring verification.

paper_title: The Bench-to-Bedside Journey of Deep Learning in Dermato-Oncology: A Systematic Review of Clinical Readiness Across the Translational Continuum
paper_abstract: Deep learning systems have matched dermatologists on curated skin cancer image sets for almost a decade, but evidence from patient care has accumulated slowly and unevenly. This systematic review mapped where that evidence now sits along the translational continuum. A reproducible PubMed search run in August 2026 identified 656 records; after single-screener selection against pre-specified criteria and full-text assessment of 39 reports, 29 clinical-stage studies (prospective, controlled, or real-world evaluations of AI for cutaneous malignancy in patients) were included and staged as prospective standalone accuracy (n = 19), prospective clinician-with-AI use (n = 5), controlled evaluation (n = 1), or real-world deployment (n = 4). Risk of bias, appraised with QUADAS-2, ROBINS-I, or JBI tools, was high or serious in 24 studies, most often because of partial verification and preselected lesion spectra, and the certainty of every principal finding was low or very low (GRADE). No included study was a randomised trial with patient outcomes, and none reported stage at diagnosis, mortality, or overdiagnosis. Across modalities, sensitivity held up in prospective use, commonly above 90% at the pre-set operating point, while specificity fell to between 9% and 85% and was frequently lower than that of the clinicians it was compared against. Performance moved with acquisition hardware, lesion spectrum, and skin type, and one market-approved dermoscopic classifier reached areas under the curve of 0.54 to 0.62 in two Australian primary care studies. One product family progressed from prospective accuracy to national-pathway deployment under a conditional health technology recommendation, with human second reading overturning a large share of automated discharges. We argue that the reported specificity loss reflects safety-first operating points, spectrum preselection, and the choice of comparator rather than model failure alone, and propose readiness criteria linking each translational stage to the evidence needed before autonomous or primary-care use. The review followed PRISMA 2020, was not registered, and received no external funding.

paper_title: BBBEE Certification as Evidence of Economic Transformation: A Systematic Review of Evidential Value for MSME Development in South Africa, 2013–2023
paper_abstract: Introduction: Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment (BBBEE) certification and compliance evaluation are intended to support economic transformation, broaden participation and improve opportunities for historically disadvantaged enterprises in South Africa. Yet certification status is not necessarily equivalent to demonstrated transformation or MSME development. This review examined how BBBEE certification and compliance evaluation relate to evidential value for economic transformation and MSME development, including associated opportunities, risks, implementation conditions and evidence gaps. Methods: The researcher-selected databases and information sources were Google Scholar, ERIC, OpenAlex, Crossref. The eligibility protocol restricted publication years to 2013–2023. COSTAQDA recorded source-level retrieval through OpenAlex (75 retrieved; 660 available), Crossref (75 retrieved; 2656 available). Where researcher-selected sources did not expose a suitable direct bulk-search connector, COSTAQDA used its OpenAlex/Crossref discovery bridge while preserving the researcher-selected source names in the PRISMA record. The identification run recorded 150 records before cross-source deduplication and 144 unique records after deduplication. Results: Five higher-order conclusions emerged. BBBEE compliance provided signals of opportunity but not consistent proof of MSME development; market access was a principal linking mechanism; outcomes depended on implementation capacity, support and contextual fit; fronting, corruption and unequal distribution weakened evidential value; and the available evidence was fragmented and insufficient for certificate-level causal evaluation. Evidence included positive perceptions, procurement access, enterprise and supplier development, skills initiatives and employee inclusion, alongside adverse or uncertain business effects and implementation failures. Discussion/Conclusion: BBBEE certification is best interpreted as an access, compliance and accountability signal rather than as standalone evidence that economic transformation or MSME development has occurred. Stronger conclusions require transparent, longitudinal and outcome-linked analysis connecting certification records with firm, beneficiary and distributional outcomes.

paper_title: A Systematic Review of Tools for Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Classification
paper_abstract: Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is one of the common mental disorders affecting children and is often diagnosed with an important delay. This neurodevelopmental disorder is usually identified by symptoms such as a deficit in attention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness. There are clinical and data-oriented methods for ADHD diagnosis. Recently, artificial intelligence techniques for ADHD diagnosis have been taken into consideration. In this article, we have reviewed state-of-the-art deep learning and classical machine learning networks using a wide range of neuroimaging, neurosignal and related data, including structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), electroencephalography (EEG), magnetoencephalography (MEG), questionnaires, genome data, mo-tion data, performance tests and game simulation. In addition, we identified common validation methods and analyzed them. As an important aspect for clinicians, the brain regions of ADHD patients identified as discriminative by existing machine learning-based studies are investigated. In the end, we identify exiting research gaps, notably the lack of publicly available large-scale multimodal datasets, non-interpretability and inexplicability of many algorithms and the use of architectures that are unable to efficiently model the spatiotemporal features of the brain. Ultimately, we hope that researchers will implement explainable machine learning-based studies that use several neuroimaging modalities to aid clinicians in supporting their decisions for diagnosis, prognosis and for treatment planning.

paper_title: Ventral Tegmental Dopamine Adaptations in Alcohol Use Disorder: A Narrative Review of Mechanisms and Prevention Implications
paper_abstract: Alcohol use disorder involves persistent changes in motivation that a uniform increase or decrease in dopamine activity cannot explain. This narrative review examines how alcohol alters ventral tegmental dopamine circuits through membrane conductances, excitatory and inhibitory inputs, and synaptic plasticity. We propose that repeated exposure can reduce baseline dopamine output while preserving or enhancing responses to alcohol and its cues. Baseline output is defined as a prespecified measurement before an event; recruitment is the event-evoked increment above that baseline. Evidence for individual adaptations is distinguished from the unproven prediction that their joint change within a defined projection contributes to renewed seeking. Withdrawal-related reward deficits, stress recruitment, receptor-specific inhibitory signaling, and selective synaptic recovery provide complementary mechanisms. Projection identity, sex, hormonal state, and dopamine release and clearance at terminals help explain differences across studies. Regional rescue experiments strengthen causal inference, but most mechanisms have not been linked selectively to relief-driven drinking or recurrence. For prevention research, these findings identify candidate processes that may support progression to persistent use and vulnerability after cessation; they do not establish clinical preventive efficacy. Priorities include longitudinal measurements within defined circuits, independent tests of reward and relief motivation, and selective physiological rescue with appropriate behavioral controls. The practical contribution is a framework for evaluating when a dopamine adaptation is a cause of vulnerability, a compensatory response, or a marker of exposure.

paper_title: Metal–Organic Framework Membranes and Adsorbents for Biogas Upgrading: A Critical Narrative Review of Process Readiness
paper_abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have tunable adsorption and transport properties, but the fact that a material performs well does not mean that the process is ready for implementation. This critical narrative review examines membrane and adsorbent results regarding CO₂/CH₄ separation and methane delivery. Literature up to 21 August 2026 has been selected and analysed according to measurement, device architectures, operating conditions and process boundaries. Membrane benefits are dependent on formulation, fabrication, pressure, humidity and contaminants. The practical value of equilibrium uptake and selectivity can be altered by the way the adsorbent is shaped, the feed and regeneration. Laboratory cycling and process modelling relate material properties to purity, recovery and energy requirements; industrial-scale and multibed scenarios remain modelled outcomes. Material composites, sequential adsorbers and membrane–adsorption trains need to be interpreted separately. Among the studies reviewed, there is no evidence of continuous household operation of an integrated MOF membrane–adsorption system. A qualitative framework links process readiness to matched controls, realistic feed conditions, complete-cycle balances and service requirements. Generalisation is limited by selection bias, shared data, incomplete reporting and unresolved source conflicts. Development should prioritise testing the intended device, durability under relevant regeneration conditions, and transparent assessment of net methane delivery, utilities and replacement.

paper_title: Beyond the Automation–Warmth Trade-Off: How Human–AI Service Configurations Shape Relational Value in Hospitality-A Critical Integrative Literature Review and Multi-Level Conceptual Framework
paper_abstract: Frontline artificial intelligence (AI) and service robotics are fundamentally transforming hospitality service encounters from traditional human-dominated touchpoints into complex, technology-infused service ecosystems. However, hospitality managers face a strategic paradox: balancing operational efficiency against relational value co-creation. Guided by Torraco's integrative review methodology, this study systematically synthesizes 29 primary source studies published across premier service management, marketing, and hospitality journals from 2004 to 2025 to reconceptualize how human–AI frontline configurations shape customer relationships. It unifies four complementary theoretical lenses: Service-Dominant Logic, Automated Social Presence Theory, the Stereotype Content Model, and the Four Intelligences Framework. It establishes a structural taxonomy of frontline configurations: AI-Led Substitution, AI-Augmented Hybrid, and Human-Led AI-Mediated encounters, and resolves three persistent empirical paradoxes. First, service robots significantly mitigate customer discomfort during awkward, embarrassing, or evaluative encounters by eliminating metaperception processing (judgment anxiety). Second, high robotic social presence is attenuated in the direct co-presence of human staff due to relative social cognition comparison penalties. Third, AI augmentation enhances customer-perceived warmth only when organizational systems convert automated time-savings into employee discretionary decision autonomy; using efficiency gains to accelerate guest throughput quotas triggers technostress, emotional exhaustion, and surface acting. Synthesizing these cognitive, affective, and organizational mechanisms into an integrative conditional process model, the study formulates six testable theoretical propositions and delineates a multi-level boundary condition matrix spanning task intelligence tiers, customer technology readiness, employee workload density, and hotel service tiers. Methodological and theoretical future research agendas are established alongside four strategic managerial directives for frontline service ecosystem design in the machine age.

paper_title: Deep Learning for Multi-Component Gearbox Fault Diagnosis on the PHM 2009 Benchmark: A Critical Review and Comparative Evaluation of Time–Frequency Representations and Network Architectures
paper_abstract: Concurrent faults in gears, bearings and shafts remain among the hardest cases for vibration-based condition monitoring of industrial gearboxes, because their signatures overlap, modulate one another and shift with speed and load. The 2009 PHM Society gearbox has become the standard public benchmark for this multi-component problem, yet published results on it are scattered across input types, network designs and validation schemes, which makes headline accuracies hard to compare. This article presents a critical review of deep-learning diagnosis on this benchmark and the wider gearbox literature, organised around three design choices: signal representation, model family and evaluation protocol. To ground the discussion, we re-analyse a controlled experiment in which three convolutional architectures were trained on 10,240 images per representation (continuous wavelet transform scalograms, short-time Fourier transform spectrograms and wavelet synchrosqueezed images) covering eight spur-gearbox health states. A compact five-stage batch-normalised network reached 99.90%, 99.85% and 99.66% test accuracy with wavelet, Synchrosqueezed and spectrogram inputs, respectively, but the margins among the best models correspond to only a few of the 2,048 test images. On a separate held-out validation subset, accuracy fell to 94.53%, 92.03% and 77.34%, making the representation effect far more visible. Comparison with published capsule-attention, architecture-search and transformer studies shows that reported accuracies on the same benchmark range from below 80% to above 99.5%, mainly because of differences in splitting protocol. We conclude with a reporting checklist and research agenda for leakage-aware, physics-informed and deployable gearbox diagnosis.

paper_title: Effects of Intermittent Fasting and Carbohydrate-Restricted Diets on Insulin Resistance and Glycemic Control Markers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
paper_abstract: Background: Intermittent fasting and carbohydrate-restricted dietary strategies have been investigated for improving insulin resistance and glycemic control, but interventions and study populations differ substantially. Objective: To summarize reported effects on fasting insulin, HOMAIR, fasting glucose, HbA1c, and the GH/IGF-1 axis in adults with excess weight or metabolic disorders. Methods: A systematic review of controlled dietary interventions was described using searches of PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar for reports published from January 2016 to March 2026. Random-effects standardized mean differences (SMDs) were transcribed from the corresponding supplementary forest plots. Results: The available plots include eight estimates for insulin (SMD -0.79; 95% CI -1.03 to -0.56; I² 22.17%), seven for HOMA-IR (-0.84; -1.10 to -0.58; I² 26.21%), 13 for fasting glucose (-0.60; -0.84 to -0.35; I² 62.66%), and seven for HbA1c (-0.81; -1.17 to -0.44; I² 64.15%). Only one study supplied GH/IGF-1 findings. The source PRISMA diagram and descriptive study table disagree on the number of included entries, preventing confirmation of a unique participant total from the supplied documents. Conclusions: The reported summaries favor lower markers of insulin resistance and glycemic exposure during the evaluated dietary interventions. Their clinical interpretation is limited by mixed protocols, incomplete outcome reporting, uncertainty about the precise within-study contrasts, and the absence of a documented study-level risk-of-bias evaluation.

paper_title: Beyond Glycaemic Control: Efficacy and Safety of Newer Antidiabetic Agents in Patients with Cardiorenal Disease—A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease are the leading causes of death in type 2 diabetes, and lowering glycated haemoglobin alone does not adequately address this risk. This narrative review summarises evidence on the glycaemic efficacy, cardiorenal outcomes and safety of sodium–glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i), glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), the dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors and once-weekly basal insulins, with attention to the Gulf region. PubMed/MEDLINE, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar were searched for trials, meta-analyses and guidelines published between 2015 and 2026. SGLT2i provide the most consistent reductions in heart failure hospitalisation and kidney disease progression, irrespective of diabetes status. GLP-1 RAs reduce major adverse cardiovascular events, stroke and kidney outcomes. Tirzepatide offers the greatest glycaemic and weight benefits, with cardiovascular protection comparable to an established GLP-1 RA. Dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors and weekly insulins are largely cardiorenal-neutral. Combining SGLT2i and GLP-1 RAs may provide additive protection. In the Middle East and North Africa, which has the highest diabetes prevalence worldwide, use of these organ-protective agents remains low. Therapy should be selected according to comorbidity, giving organ protection the same priority as glycaemic control.

paper_title: Gut Microbiota and Immune Mechanisms in Primary Hypertension in Children: A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Primary hypertension (PH) in children is an increasingly prevalent multifactorial disorder involving complex interactions between genetic, metabolic, neurohormonal, immune, and environmental factors. Recent studies highlight the potential role of gut microbiota composition and immune dysregulation in the development and progression of PH and hypertension-mediated organ damage (HMOD) in children. The gut microbiota strongly influences immune responses and vascular function through its metabolites, such as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), which help maintain the intestinal barrier and modulate inflammation. Conversely, dysbiosis, defined as reduced microbial diversity and increased proinflammatory taxa, can exacerbate systemic inflammation and hypertension. Immune mechanisms, including T helper 17 (Th17) cell polarization and impaired regulatory T cell (Treg) function, facilitate sodium retention, endothelial dysfunction, and organ remodeling. This narrative review summarizes current knowledge of gut microbiota alterations and immunological pathways in pediatric PH, emphasizing the potential of inflammatory markers as early biomarkers. The review also discusses how lifestyle factors such as diet and physical activity modify the gut microbiota-immune axis and blood pressure regulation. Additionally, the study highlights gaps in current knowledge and possible directions for further research. Understanding these pathways offers promising opportunities for early diagnosis, risk stratification, and novel therapeutic interventions to prevent long-term cardiovascular complications in hypertensive children.

paper_title: AI Literacy and Migrant Rights Information in Bangladesh: A Survey of AI Aware Respondents
paper_abstract: Accurate and accessible information can help people navigating overseas employment, while generative artificial intelligence (AI) creates new questions about the quality and verification of migration-related advice. This study examines responses to statements about AI literacy and migrant-worker-rights information in 385 adult, AI-aware survey records from Bangladesh. The mixed sample includes law students, graduates, legal professionals and other respondents; prospective overseas workers are not identified in the workbook. The questionnaire asks about self-reported ability to locate rights information with AI, recognition of the need to verify migration information, awareness of misleading recruitment information and support for pre-departure AI-literacy training. It does not test knowledge of specific migrant-worker rights or observe use of an AI migration service. Item distributions, joint endorsement, paired comparisons and exploratory ordinal correlations are reported. Of 385 respondents, 256 (66.5%) endorsed the ability-to-locate statement, 341 (88.6%) endorsed the need to verify AI-generated migration information, and 267 (69.4%) supported AI-literacy training in pre-departure preparation. A total of 231 respondents (60.0%) endorsed both locating information and the need for verification; 110 endorsed verification without endorsing locating information. These answers do not establish actual verification or training effectiveness. The article distinguishes locating information, verifying its authority, knowing a legal right and obtaining an effective remedy. Future research should identify prospective workers, use rights-specific scenarios and document recruitment and consent procedures.

paper_title: Investigating the Effectiveness of Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment Programmes in Supporting MSMEs in South Africa: A Systematic Review
paper_abstract: Introduction: Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment (B-BBEE) is intended to advance participation, enterprise development, supplier development, skills development and transformation in South Africa. Its contribution to the growth, performance and sustainability of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), however, remains contested. The supplied literature includes evidence of perceived benefits, developmental opportunities, resource constraints, compliance burdens and weak institutional implementation. Methods: The researcher-selected databases and information sources were Google Scholar and ERIC. The eligibility protocol restricted publication years to 2016–2026. The exact calendar date of search execution was not recorded in the verified identification provenance; this is distinct from the publication-year eligibility range. The review searched Google Scholar and ERIC using a predefined Boolean strategy covering MSMEs, B-BBEE mechanisms and enterprise outcomes, with publication eligibility restricted to 2016–2026. Results: B-BBEE appears most enabling when enterprise and supplier development is embedded in productive value chains, knowledge transfer, skills development and inter-organisational collaboration. Benefits are constrained by limited finance, collateral, infrastructure, market access, technical knowledge, planning and management capability. Legislative change, compliance complexity, weak communication, fragmented institutional support, corruption and fronting risks can displace substantive transformation. Perceptions of benefit coexist with weakly demonstrated direct effects on MSME growth and sustainability. Evidence is heterogeneous and direct longitudinal outcome evidence is limited. Discussion/Conclusion: B-BBEE should be understood as conditionally effective rather than uniformly successful or unsuccessful. Its developmental contribution depends on contextual inclusion, measurable outcomes, coordinated implementation, enterprise capability building and accountability. Stronger longitudinal and MSME-specific evaluations are required to establish causal effects on revenue, employment, productivity, survival and sustainability.

paper_title: Training–Rollout Mismatch in Low-Precision LLM Reinforcement Learning: A Survey
paper_abstract: Low-precision rollouts can reduce the cost of reinforcement learning for large language models, but numerical discrepancies between the sampler and learner can compromise policy optimization. Even with synchronized parameters and identical token histories, the two execution paths may assign different token probabilities, altering gradient estimation and update decisions. This survey examines how training–rollout mismatch arises, propagates through policy optimization, and evolves over training. We develop a component-level taxonomy that organizes existing approaches by intervention target into two complementary families: numerical design, which aligns execution across learner and sampler paths or preserves numerical fidelity and update visibility; and learning under residual mismatch, which corrects gradient estimation or controls policy updates. We compare the mechanisms, information requirements, and residual errors of these interventions to explain their limitations and how they can be combined. We further synthesize measurement practices and experimental evidence across precision regimes, architectures, and training configurations, examining how numerical discrepancies affect optimization stability, policy improvement, and computational cost. We clarify how differences in policy pairs, metric definitions, and training horizons shape the interpretation of reported results. Open challenges include predicting harmful mismatch, reducing mitigation overhead, sustaining policy improvement over longer training, and comparing methods at matched quality or end-to-end cost.

paper_title: Conformal Annotation with Randomized Expert Review: Application to Online Cell-Type Labeling
paper_abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) models can accelerate cell-type annotation in digital pathology, but safely scaling their use requires determining, with error control, which model-generated labels can be accepted without expert review. This is challenging in evolving workflows because cell morphology and type composition may change across tissue regions and slides, making one-time calibration unreliable. We propose Conformal Annotation with Randomized Expert review under Distribution shift (CARED), a distribution-free framework that leverages randomized expert audit to achieve long-run error control for AI-assisted annotation under distribution shift. For each incoming batch, CARED uniformly selects a subset of cases for expert review and uses the acquired labels to calibrate later decisions. Among unreviewed cases, CARED determines a subset of them to safely skip expert labeling, while suggesting candidate labels for the others for downstream resolution. We prove that this workflow provides long-run control of cumulative error over both the full stream and the cells outside of the audit sample, without stationarity or exchangeability assumptions. We further enhance the framework by introducing class-conditional guarantees to ensure error control within important but rare cell types, together with a utility module to target more automatic resolutions, smaller candidate sets, and greater biological coherence, without compromising validity. Experiments on pancreas, lung, and ovary annotation streams, together with a stream constructed from real expert annotations, show that CARED controls the cumulative errors while a substantial fraction of cells (up to 70%) bypass expert review.

paper_title: Towards Human-Centered Safety in Vision-Language-Action Robot Control: A Survey and Outlook
paper_abstract: As Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models couple perception and language understanding with physical action in human-shared environments, safety depends on whether they capture relevant information about people, environments, and social context and use it to shape robot behavior. We therefore center this survey on semantic-to-action causality towards human-centered robot safety, examining how safety-relevant semantics remain consequential for actions that preserve human well-being, environmental integrity, and social compliance. To trace this relationship from learning through execution to validation, we organize the literature across design-time methods that shape how safety-relevant features are learned, deployment-time mechanisms that govern their influence on behavior, and validation-time approaches that assess their effectiveness under safety-critical conditions. Across these stages, we identify four linked requirements, safety boundary coverage, semantic-to-action fidelity, contextual intervention and recovery, and incident-path validation, which describe how safety-relevant information must be captured, preserved, enforced, and evidenced. These requirements expose corresponding open challenges in sparse boundary examples, limited causal verifiability, gaps in intervention timing and recovery, and incomplete incident attribution.

paper_title: When Satisfaction and Clinical Outcome Disagree: Understanding Discordance Between Patient Experience and Psychiatric Treatment Response—A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Patient satisfaction and patient-reported experience are widely used as indicators of the quality of mental health care and, implicitly, as proxies for treatment benefit, whereas clinical outcome is usually judged from clinician-rated symptom scales. This narrative review examines whether, and why, these two assessments diverge in psychiatric treatment. It clarifies the constructs of satisfaction, experience and outcome; examines measurement- and rater-level sources of apparent disagreement; synthesises studies that directly compare patient- and clinician-derived assessments; and proposes an explanatory framework. Associations between satisfaction and clinician-rated outcome are consistently positive but small: in one acute-care study, experience of care accounted for less than 7% of the variance in symptom change, and patient–clinician agreement about the same care episode was low. Patients and clinicians judge improvement from different frames of reference, while ceiling effects, social desirability and fixed thresholds for meaningful change further distort comparison. Seven mechanisms sustain divergence: expectancy, therapeutic alliance, insight, subjective tolerability, decisional involvement, perceived coercion and the conceptual gap between symptom remission and personal recovery; each shapes satisfaction largely independently of symptom change. Satisfaction and clinical outcome are therefore related but non-interchangeable constructs. Services should measure both, adjust satisfaction scores for patient characteristics, and treat discordance as clinically informative rather than as error. Shared decision-making, honest expectation management, reduction of perceived coercion and recovery-oriented care are the most plausible routes to aligning patient experience with clinical outcome.

paper_title: Mirtazapine-Associated Seizures in a 15-Year-Old Adolescent and a Case-Based Systematic Review
paper_abstract: Purpose: To present a case of mirtazapine associated seizures in an adolescent boy and to conduct a systematic review of published cases of seizures occurring in association with mirtazapine use. Methods: We presented our case and conducted a systematic search, following the PRISMA Statement, in the PubMed and Scopus databases for mirtazapine associated seizure cases, until 12th September 2026. Results: A 15-year-old patient arrived at the emergency department of our hospital via ambulance due to a generalized tonic-clonic seizure occurring 15 minutes prior. The toxicology report of his urine sample was positive for mirtazapine metabolites. He was self-administering mirtazapine for an unknown amount of time. This was the most likely cause of the generalized tonic-clonic seizures. No further seizures occurred during hospitalization. Our systematic search yielded 7 published cases. The median age was 50 years. The dosage of mirtazapine ranged from 7.5 mg to 60 mg per day. Excluding one case with an overdose, seizures presented a few days after mirtazapine initiation or dosage escalation—three cases presented with focal seizures and 3 cases with generalized seizures. Two cases had a positive history of epilepsy, and 4 cases were on other medications that can lower the seizure threshold. In most cases, withdrawal of mirtazapine was sufficient for seizure resolution. Conclusion: The available evidence cannot establish a causative relationship between mirtazapine and seizures. The temporal association observed in several cases suggests that physicians should remain vigilant for seizure occurrence, particularly in individuals with pre-existing epilepsy or other potential seizure risk factors.

paper_title: Evaluating Quantized Language Model Inference a Critical Review of Quality Memory and Workload Tradeoffs
paper_abstract: Quantization reduces the numerical precision of large language model weights, activations, or key-value caches, but its practical value depends on the interaction among numerical error, workload, and execution hardware. This review compares representative methods through those three dimensions. A purposive literature synthesis covers integer inference foundations, outlier-aware mixed precision, second-order weight reconstruction, activation-aware scaling, rotations, cache quantization, and training with low-bit representations. Rather than pool incompatible benchmark results, the review distinguishes the object being quantized, the required preparation, the retained precision, and the implementation needed for a benefit. An analytical memory model separates compressed weights from quantization metadata, caches, and runtime workspace. A recomputable worked example and concurrency sensitivity analysis show why a fourfold reduction in nominal weight bytes does not imply a fourfold reduction in total serving memory. The paper proposes a reproducible comparison protocol that separates prefill from decoding and evaluates quality, latency distributions, throughput, peak memory, and amortized preparation cost under a common workload. It also distinguishes quantized fine-tuning from inference optimization and native low-bit training from post-training conversion. No new model benchmark, speedup, or accuracy result is reported. The central conclusion is that quantization should be selected against an application-specific operating envelope, with quality constraints and hardware measurements, rather than ranked by bit width alone.

paper_title: Taif Roses: Historical Richness, Modern Industrial Vitality, and Global Reach—An Integrative Evidence Review, 2000–2026
paper_abstract: Taif rose (Rosa damascena Mill. var. trigintipetala) is the defining crop of the Taif highlands of Saudi Arabia, a heritage practice inscribed by UNESCO in 2024 and a working industry whose farms, distilleries, and residue streams have only recently become objects of systematic study. This integrative review assembles the peer-reviewed evidence published between 2000 and 2026 and reads it against three claims embedded in the crop’s public identity: that it has a rich history, that it sustains a thriving modern industry, and that it holds a global presence. Crossref and OpenAlex were searched on October 15, 2026; 727 records were screened against verified bibliographic metadata, and 39 studies met the inclusion criteria. Findings were analyzed through reflexive thematic analysis and interpreted using the Evidence-Based Field-to-Formulation (EFF) framework developed here, which combines value-chain, circular-bioeconomy, translational-evidence, and place-based quality lenses over a digital enabling layer. Five themes emerged: chemical identity and terroir; bioactivity and safety; circular valorization of residues; propagation, stress physiology, and plant health; and digital and process innovation. The evidence confirms a measurable place-based chemical identity, a substantial and partly characterized residue stream, and a maturing propagation toolkit. It does not yet support the industry’s highest-value claims: no study has tested Taif rose material in humans, origin authentication remains unvalidated, and one included-adjacent study was retracted during the review. Taif rose is historically rich and industrially active, but its global presence is cultural and commercial rather than evidential. Closing that gap requires authentication science, safe residue routing, and early-phase clinical research.

paper_title: From Waste to Resource: Characterization, Management, and Resource Recovery of Electrocoagulation Sludge in Mine Tailings Water Treatment: A Structured Review
paper_abstract: Electrocoagulation (EC) treatment of mine tailings water transfers metals, metalloids, and suspended minerals into sludge, creating a secondary waste stream whose resource potential requires rigorous qualification. This structured review synthesizes 105 eligible studies selected from 850 Scopus records published during 2006–2026; search and screening records are documented in Supplementary Material S1. Evidence from mine-affected waters is distinguished from non-mining wastewater studies, whose recovery outcomes require matrix-specific validation before transfer to tailings-derived sludge. Investigated pathways include sludge conditioning, adsorption, catalysis, construction materials, pigments, and selective mineral recovery. Across these applications, aqueous contaminant removal, solid-phase formation, functional performance, and environmental safety represent distinct evidentiary requirements. We propose a source–phase–function–risk (SPFR) framework linking feedwater and electrode provenance, mineralogical and chemical phase identity, application-specific performance benchmarks, contaminant mobility, and life-cycle and techno-economic comparisons. SPFR provides a transparent, staged qualification approach rather than a validated predictive score. Key research priorities include dry-solid mass balances, phase-resolved characterization, product durability, realistic leaching and aging tests, and consistent functional-unit comparisons. These requirements support evidence-based decisions on responsible resource recovery from EC sludge generated during mine tailings water treatment.

paper_title: Oak Galls (Quercus infectoria, Manjakani) in Women's Intimate Health: A Critical Review of the Clinical Evidence, Effects on the Vaginal Ecosystem and Safety
paper_abstract: Oak galls, known in Malaysia and Indonesia as manjakani, are traditionally used for vaginal discharge, laxity and postpartum care, and are widely sold in feminine washes and tightening products. A 2023 systematic review of oak gall phytochemistry and bioactivity did not address these uses. This review examines the clinical evidence for oak gall in female genital conditions, its likely effects on the vaginal ecosystem, and its safety by route of use. One double-blind randomised trial found similar short-term cure of bacterial vaginosis with an oak gall cream and metronidazole gel (82.1% versus 87.5%), but it was not designed to show equivalence and did not assess recurrence. No trial supports tightening claims. Gall extracts inhibit Lactobacillus acidophilus at the same concentrations as pathogens, regular douching increases bacterial vaginosis risk, and intravaginal tightening products have been associated with HIV acquisition. Repeated oral dosing of a gall extract caused organ lesions and reduced thyroid hormones in rats at 500 mg/kg/day, and tannic acid absorbed through damaged tissue has caused fatal liver necrosis. Reported tannic acid contents above 1000 mg/g also show that quantification needs validation. Oak gall products should be limited to external use until microbiota, irritation and recurrence data are available.

paper_title: A Survey of Agentic Robotics: Toward Continual Self-Improvement
paper_abstract: Foundation models (FMs), particularly large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs), are increasingly used as the decision-making core of AI agents and are now being extended from digital environments to robotic systems. In classical robotics, engineers decompose tasks, specify objectives, write control code, and repair failures before deployment; in agentic robotics, an FM makes some of these decisions at run time or during improvement. Bringing this paradigm into the physical world introduces additional challenges: FM-mediated decisions must be grounded in executable robot behavior, respect physical constraints, and close the loop through real-world feedback. We survey this emerging paradigm and organize existing systems by three loci of FM-mediated agency: task orchestration, motion/action generation, and improvement. Coding rules for each locus make the definition operational, including a test of which improvement decisions the FM makes that separates fixed-procedure from agent-directed improvement. We apply these rules to the systems retrieved by a systematic search, examine verification and feedback-closure mechanisms, and compare what self-improving systems have demonstrated. Finally, we discuss continual self-improvement as a central emerging frontier and the challenges toward reliable autonomous improvement through physical interaction.

paper_title: Regenerative Economy and Sustainable Development: A Scoping Review of Concepts, Strategies, Measurement and Gaps
paper_abstract: Regeneration has moved into economics and management as a proposal to go beyond reducing harm and strengthen the capacity of social-ecological systems to renew themselves, but the field lacks consolidation. This scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) mapped the definitions, strategies, measurement approaches and gaps of the regenerative economy. Searches in three sources and citation chasing identified 2273 records; after screening with blind reliability checks, 165 peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2026 were charted. Definitions converge on the health of living systems (59%), net positive contributions (57%) and co-evolution with place (48%), and 88% contrast regeneration with sustainability, but only 8% distinguish it from corporate social responsibility. Social regeneration and policy (50% each) are the most frequent strategies, whereas cultural aspects receive less attention. Measurement is the main weakness: 59% of documents report no measurement approach, 16% only propose metrics and only 4% (8% of empirical studies) measure observed ecological, social or economic outcomes, while baselines, thresholds and additionality are rarely declared. Developing economies host more than half of the located studies, but global frameworks come mainly from authors in developed economies. The review proposes a verifiable definition, a checklist for regenerative claims and a research agenda linked to organisational innovation.

paper_title: Creative Assignments and Who Gets Left Behind: A Systematic Review of Inclusion Readiness in Generative AI Teaching Practices in Business and Technology Higher Education
paper_abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) assignments are spreading rapidly in business and technology higher education, yet published accounts rarely report whether every student can take part on fair terms. This systematic review audited published GenAI assignments against the social, economic, institutional and environmental dimensions of pedagogical sustainability. Following PRISMA 2020, OpenAlex (2023–2026) was searched, 1092 peer-reviewed records were screened and 191 studies were included. Each assignment was coded for its creative family, access and fairness provisions, ethics content and assessment, and scored on a 0–5 inclusion-readiness index. An AI system served as primary coder; a human coder double-coded 30 studies and the author adjudicated all disagreements. Most assignments used GenAI as a tutor or thinking partner (52%). Provisions were scarce: 27% ensured free access, 2% offered a non-AI alternative task and 2% addressed disability. Privacy (53%) and opt-out (35%) appeared mainly as research-ethics safeguards rather than design features. Mean inclusion readiness was 1.30 of 5 (0.75 on design-only coding). Only one study in seven taught GenAI ethics, and environmental cost was taught once. Business courses favored choice and language support; technology courses favored central access. The index offers a measurable design and reporting checklist for sustainable GenAI pedagogy.

paper_title: Towards Task-Oriented Semantic Communication: A Survey on Technologies, Opportunities, and Challenges
paper_abstract: The growing demand for intelligent and adaptive services is accelerating the transition from conventional communication systems to semantic communication. Task-Oriented Semantic Communication (ToSC) has emerged as an efficient framework that reduces communication cost by transmitting only task-relevant information for downstream processing. This survey reviews the theoretical foundations, system architectures, and enabling technologies of ToSC, providing a taxonomy of design strategies spanning collaborative edge inference, end-to-end optimization, and multi-agent cooperation. Key technologies, including deep learning-based semantic representation and adaptive joint source-channel coding, are discussed. Device heterogeneity and partial observability are examined alongside recent tasks' performance evaluations, such as classification and recognition. The survey also discusses the integration of large-scale multimodal foundation models into semantic encoders for zero-shot task adaptation, continual learning frameworks for on-device semantic processing, cooperative multi-agent reasoning with interpretable information exchange, and cross-layer co-design within AI-native 6G infrastructures, leveraging reconfigurable intelligent surfaces and digital twins. By consolidating existing knowledge and identifying key design trade-offs in latency, accuracy, and bandwidth efficiency, this work aims to serve as both a reference and a roadmap for advancing ToSC toward reliable and resource-efficient communication in 6G and beyond.

paper_title: Polymeric Binders for Metal Binder Jetting Additive Manufacturing: A Review
paper_abstract: In metal Binder Jetting Additive Manufacturing (BJAM), the polymeric binder is often treated as a temporary, almost incidental consumable — yet it silently governs nearly every outcome of the process, from droplet ejection to the properties of the final sintered part. This review reframes the binder as a central design variable and examines it through a polymer-science lens, tracing its influence along the complete BJAM process chain. We first dissect binder chemistry and architecture, organizing aqueous, solvent-based, and reactive systems by carrier medium and bonding mechanism, and linking molecular features — functional groups, chain entanglement, and crosslinking — to printability, green strength, and clean thermal removal. We then follow the binder into the powder bed, where rheology, droplet dynamics, and capillary migration dictate spreading, penetration, and shape fidelity; into the green part, where adhesion and particle bridging set mechanical integrity; and through debinding and sintering, where decomposition chemistry, residual carbon, and densification determine final quality. A survey of automotive, energy, aerospace, biomedical, and tooling applications highlights where binder limitations still constrain industrial adoption. Throughout, we emphasize the recurring trade-offs — jettability versus green strength, penetration versus saturation, and burnout cleanliness versus chemical composition — that any next-generation binder must resolve, and we outline design criteria toward predictive, application-specific binder development.

paper_title: Large Language Models in Product Design: A Review
paper_abstract: Product design is a complex, knowledge-based process that balances customer needs with engineering constraints and market realities. While traditional methods such as Quality Function Deployment (QFD) and machine learning (ML) have improved the design process and solutions, they still struggle with flexibility and a deep semantic understanding of design requirements. Advances in Large Language Models (LLMs), powered by Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), create new opportunities for intelligent, human-centred support for product design. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this systematic review analyzes 1,263 studies published between 2023 and 2026 to answer three questions: (1) how LLMs are applied across design stages, (2) how these systems are evaluated, and (3) what gaps remain. We found that LLMs successfully support design requirements analysis, ideation, and documentation. However, current evaluation methods lack standardized benchmarks for design quality. Persistent challenges remain, including hallucinations, weak domain grounding, tool-integration hurdles, and ethical concerns. To guide future research, we introduce a technical maturity map that highlights current achievements and uninvestigated areas in design systems and suggests a roadmap for applying LLMs in product design.

paper_title: Centella asiatica and Butterfly Pea (Clitoria ternatea) in Oral Beauty Supplements and Functional Beverages: A Critical Review of Human Evidence, Bioavailability, Safety and Formulation
paper_abstract: Centella asiatica and butterfly pea (Clitoria ternatea) are increasingly combined in oral beauty supplements and blue-coloured functional beverages in Asia. A 2026 randomised trial reported that oral Centella extract reduced wrinkle depth, and a 2023 review proposed microencapsulated butterfly pea extract as a functional food ingredient. This review examines the human evidence, bioavailability, safety and formulation of both ingredients for these products. The Centella trial met its primary endpoint, a 3.9 µm greater reduction in average wrinkle depth than placebo with 14 mg of asiaticoside a day, but it was registered retrospectively, analysed per protocol, run by the manufacturer and contains internal inconsistencies, and its secondary effects were below 3%. Parent Centella triterpenes reach very low plasma concentrations, and three cases of hepatitis, one with positive rechallenge, have been reported in women of the same age. Butterfly pea has no human skin data; small acute trials show post-meal glucose, lipid and antioxidant effects. It is permitted in the United States as a colour additive, but the European Food Safety Authority objected to dried flowers as a traditional food because of cyclotides. Microencapsulation studies measured colour and antioxidant assays, not bioavailability. Products should claim no more than this evidence supports.

paper_title: Bone Replacement Grafts in Periodontal Regeneration: Biologically Active Materials or Space-Maintaining Scaffolds? A Critical Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Bone replacement grafts are widely used in periodontal regenerative surgery, yet their specific contribution to periodontal tissue regeneration remains uncertain. This critical narrative review examines evidence published through September 2026 on autogenous bone, allografts, xenografts, and alloplasts for periodontal intrabony defects, prioritizing randomized controlled trials, and human histological studies. The synthesis considers comparative efficacy, defect morphology, combination therapies, and discrepancies between clinical, radiographic, and histological outcomes. Regenerative approaches generally improve clinical attachment outcomes compared with open flap debridement; however, evidence does not establish the consistent superiority of any graft category. Defect depth, angle, and residual-wall configuration are associated with treatment response. Clinical attachment gain and radiographic defect fill do not necessarily demonstrate regeneration of the complete periodontal attachment apparatus. Autogenous bone may supply osteogenic cells, whereas selected demineralized allografts have preparation-dependent osteoinductive potential. Xenografts and most alloplasts appear to contribute predominantly through osteoconduction, clot stabilization, and space maintenance. Additional benefits from biologics or barrier membranes vary with defect characteristics and surgical context. Thus, many substitutes may act principally as permissive scaffolds supporting host-mediated regeneration. Graft selection should reflect defect-specific biological and mechanical requirements rather than presumed intrinsic regenerative potency.

paper_title: Beyond Passing Tests: A Systematic Review and Controlled Re-evaluation of Techniques for Improving the Quality of LLM-Generated Code
paper_abstract: Large language models pass most functional-correctness benchmarks, but passing tests says little about whether their code is readable, efficient or secure. Many techniques claim to improve these qualities, yet their evidence is scattered, usually covers one quality dimension and is rarely compared at an equal compute budget. We contribute a systematic review and a controlled re-evaluation. A systematic literature review of 628 primary studies (July 2021 to October 2026), with disclosed, author-reviewed LLM assistance, organizes the techniques by stage, signal source and quality target. Most studies measure only the dimension they target, gains often come with unchanged or unreported correctness, single automated quality signals are gamed, and compute, variance and contamination are rarely reported. A controlled re-evaluation runs ten techniques on four models at matched budgets on correctness, maintainability, efficiency and security benchmarks, extends it to thirteen current models and repository-level tasks, and compares 66 highlighted techniques head-to-head on Gemma 4 31B. At one call, quality prompting raises analyzer issue counts and leaves complexity and judge scores almost unchanged. At matched budgets, best-of-n sampling with an analyzer-weighted ranker matches or beats prompting, planning, self-refinement, a reviewer agent and retrieval on measures the ranker does not optimize, while an analyzer feedback loop and fine-tuning beat it only on analyzer issue counts. Large correctness losses on HumanEval+, a likely contaminated benchmark near its ceiling, do not appear on contests held after the models' training cutoffs. In the head-to-head, 1 of 66 techniques beats best-of-n on its primary target beyond the 95% interval, a rate consistent with chance. Gains should be reported against a budget-matched sampling baseline and on measures independent of the technique's own signal.
comments: 55 pages, 5 figures, plus 120 pages of supplementary material

paper_title: Trustworthy Distributed Machine Learning in Cloud-Edge-IoT Systems: A Heterogeneity-Aware Survey of Security, Privacy, and Robustness
paper_abstract: Distributed machine learning (DML), including conventional distributed training and federated learning (FL), enables collaborative model development across cloud-edge-IoT systems without fully centralizing raw data. However, distributing data, computation, updates, and orchestration increases the attack surface and introduces coupled challenges across privacy, robustness, reliability, fairness, and governance. This survey presents a security-centered, heterogeneity-aware roadmap for trustworthy DML, with FL treated as a prominent high-risk case. We first characterize the assets, adversaries, trust assumptions, and coordination patterns that define DML/FL security boundaries. We then analyze how statistical, system, and trust heterogeneity, including non-IID data, resource asymmetry, intermittent participation, and cross-silo/cross-device trust differences, affect convergence, fairness, attack detectability, and defense reliability. Next, we synthesize attack-defense interactions across poisoning, backdoors, Byzantine manipulation, privacy leakage, model extraction, network/orchestration attacks, Sybil behavior, and strategic participation. We further compare layered defenses, including robust aggregation, drift-aware optimization, differential privacy, secure aggregation, homomorphic encryption, secure multiparty computation, trusted execution environments, watermarking, provenance, authenticated communication, and monitoring. Finally, we discuss deployment, evaluation, governance, and open research guidelines, emphasizing reproducible, non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) partitions, attack-aware benchmarks, privacy budgets, attack success rate, client-level disparity, latency, communication, memory, energy/carbon overhead, and auditable lifecycle artifacts.

paper_title: When AI performs, what remains? An integrative review of generative AI and cognitive capital in individuals and organizations
paper_abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is rapidly entering knowledge work, and its short-term productivity benefits are increasingly documented. Less is known about what happens, over time, to the knowledge, skills and judgment that remain in people and organizations. This integrative narrative review addresses that question through the construct of cognitive capital: the accumulated, renewable and depletable stock of knowledge, cognitive and metacognitive capabilities, and practices that enables an individual or an organization to learn, interpret information, exercise judgment, solve problems and adapt. We distinguish individual and organizational cognitive capital from the capability of the human-AI system, so that gains in joint performance and losses in human capability can be observed at the same time. Drawing on experimental, field and conceptual work, we propose four mechanisms through which interaction with AI affects cognitive capital: substitution of practice, scaffolding and feedback, metacognitive calibration, and organizational aggregation. Seven principles summarize the current evidence, including that assisted performance differs from retained competence, that the same technology can support or displace learning depending on design and use, and that individual gains can coexist with reduced collective diversity. For each mechanism we derive testable propositions, and we discuss five design levers for organizations as proposals to be validated rather than established practice. We conclude that cognitive capital offers a multilevel frame for governing AI adoption and outline a research agenda centered on longitudinal, multilevel measurement.

paper_title: Documenting Continuum of Gut Health Measures from Health to Disease: A Review of Scientific Literature and Patient-Facing Information
paper_abstract: Gut health is recognized as an important contributor to overall health, yet there is no widely accepted definition or standardized approach to its measurement. This work aimed to characterize how gut health is measured and described across academic research and patient-facing materials, and to evaluate available evidence on reliability and validity of commonly used measures. A systematic review of the literature since 2011 was conducted to identify measures of gut health used in human studies; a review of selected medical association materials was also completed to assess how gut health is communicated to in potential patient-facing materials. Measures were categorized across domains of symptoms, function, integrity, and immunity, and a targeted review of reliability and validity of the different tools and measurements identified from the systematic literature review was performed. Substantial heterogeneity in how gut health is conceptualized and measured was observed and gut health was rarely defined. While a broad range of tools and measurements are available and there is good evidence for their overall reliability and validity, there is a lack of evidence supporting their reliability and validity specific to gut health. This review provides a foundation for identifying candidate measures and gaps in validation for defining gut health.

paper_title: Multimodal Preoperative Care in Paediatric Surgery: Prehabilitation and Medical Optimisation—A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Prehabilitation, traditionally defined as a trimodal approach combining nutritional support, physical exercise, and psychological support, has been shown to improve nutritional status, reduce postoperative complications, and shorten hospital stays in adults. However, direct extrapolation of adult prehabilitation programmes to paediatric care is inappropriate, as nutritional priorities in children extend beyond preoperative optimisation to supporting adequate growth and development. Furthermore, paediatric patients differ considerably in age, developmental stage, and type of surgery, requiring interventions tailored to individual needs. Medical optimisation, although not strictly a component of prehabilitation, is closely linked to Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways. Therefore, this narrative review proposes a multimodal approach to preoperative care in children, encompassing four key components: nutrition, physical exercise, psychological support, and medical optimisation. We review the rationale, available evidence, and practical considerations for each component in children undergoing surgery. Successful implementation requires a multidisciplinary team, including surgeons, anaesthetists, nurses, dietitians, physiotherapists, psychologists, and occupational therapists, with active involvement of caregivers throughout the process. Although paediatric prehabilitation is promising, the available evidence remains limited. Well-designed clinical trials assessing clinically relevant outcomes are needed to establish the effectiveness and safety of individual interventions.

paper_title: Clinical and Molecular Characterization of Hereditary Sensory and Autonomic Neuropathy [HSAN] - Type IV.- A Narrative Literature Review
paper_abstract: Hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type IV [HSAN IV] is a rare ge-netic disorder of children characterized by the inability to feel pain and to sweat [anhidrosis]. There is insensitivity to temperature. Dysfunction of the sensory nerves which are responsible for pain and temperature causes the sensory loss. NTRK1 gene variants cause this disorder, inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern. This review aims to synthesize current research on the clinical, molecular, and diagnostic aspects of Hereditary Sensory and Autonomic Neuropathy -IV [HSAN IV] and identify gaps for future research. The objectives include reviewing studies on HSAN's clinical features and genetic variations, assessing the effectiveness of diagnostic methods, genetic testing and highlighting inconsist-encies in genotype-phenotype correlations. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase and Google Scholar using terms 'HSAN' and 'genetic vari-ants', with no time frame restrictions. The literature on the clinical and molec-ular characteristics, diagnostics, therapeutics including recent advances of HSAN IV has been reviewed. This review highlights advancements in understanding HSAN's clinical and genetic aspects, while emphasizing the need for further re-search to address gaps in genetic knowledge and improve diagnosis and treatment outcomes.

paper_title: Marked Variation in the Diagnosis and Management of Sarcoidosis Across Europe: Results from a Multinational Expert Survey
paper_abstract: Background: Sarcoidosis is a highly heterogeneous disease, leading to differences in clinical practices across countries. This study aimed to identify similarities and differences in diagnostic, therapeutic, and follow-up practices for sarcoidosis across European coun-tries. Methods: Within the Joint Action on REspiratory Diseases (JARED) project, we conducted a multinational, cross-sectional study using a key informant expert survey. The structured survey comprised 48 questions on adult sarcoidosis diagnostics and management. Rep-resentatives of all 15 JARED project countries completed the electronic survey. Results: Sarcoidosis and/or interstitial lung disease centres are present in 12 countries, but only 7 have national guidelines for diagnosis and treatment. In most countries, bron-choscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage and endobronchial ultrasound-guided lymph node biopsy are performed. The use of bronchoscopic lung biopsies, particularly cryo-biopsies, varies considerably. To assess the extent and activity of the disease, almost all countries perform extended pulmonary function testing, but there are variations in the use of hypercalcaemia and hypercalciuria tests. Positron emission tomography is used routinely only in 4 countries. Around half of the patients are treated with corticosteroids. In most cases, treatment is initiated when an organ other than the lungs is affected or when severe pulmonary function impairment is present. The follow-up intervals range from 1 to 12 months. The monitoring strategies vary based on the radiological stage of sarcoidosis or the severity of the disease. Conclusions: Our survey highlights substantial variation in sarcoidosis management across Europe, underscoring the need for updated, evidence-based recommendations on diagnostic strategies, treatment initiation and duration, and long-term follow-up.

paper_title: Co-Pyrolysis of Biomass with Plastic, Waste Tire, and Sewage Sludge for Sustainable Fuel Production: A Review
paper_abstract: The escalating global demand for sustainable energy and the environmental burden of organic and synthetic waste have intensified interest in co-pyrolysis, a thermochemical process that simultaneously converts biomass and various waste materials into valuable fuels and chemicals. This review presents an up-to-date, factorial analysis of co-pyrolysis systems, emphasizing synergistic interactions between lignocellulosic and non-lignocellulosic biomass, such as plastics, tires, sewage sludge, and other waste streams. The study systematically examines key factors such as feedstock properties, thermal decomposition mechanisms, and operational parameters (e.g., temperature, heating rate, residence time, particle size, and mixing ratio). It also highlights catalyst development, including zeolite- and biochar-based systems, to enhance product yield, aromatic selectivity, and hydrogen production while reducing oxygenated compounds. The review also discusses emerging trends in bio-oil upgrading techniques and advanced characterization protocols to address challenges in stability, acidity, and fuel applicability. We also review integrating co-pyrolysis with renewable technologies and artificial intelligence tools for predictive modeling, process optimization, and system scalability. Despite promising advances, critical gaps remain in mechanistic understanding, catalyst deactivation, long-term process viability, and comprehensive techno-economic and lifecycle assessments. This review offers actionable insights for researchers, engineers, and policymakers, providing a strategic roadmap to advance co-pyrolysis technologies toward industrial-scale implementation in a circular, low-carbon energy economy.

paper_title: Data Centers and Large Loads in Power Systems: A Comprehensive Review of Modeling, Applications, and Industry Practices
paper_abstract: The rapid growth of large electricity-consuming facilities, including hyperscale data centers, hydrogen electrolyzers, cryptocurrency mining operations, electric vehicle charging hubs, and electrified industrial processes, is introducing new challenges for transmission planning and power system reliability. Unlike traditional aggregated loads, many emerging large loads are highly concentrated, exhibit rapid power variations, and increasingly rely on power-electronic interfaces, resulting in dynamic behaviors that are not adequately represented by conventional load models. Consequently, accurate load modeling has become essential for steady-state analysis, stability assessment, interconnection studies, and long-term transmission planning. This paper presents a comprehensive review of large load modeling methodologies and their applications in future transmission planning. The evolution of load modeling is examined from classical static ZIP models and induction motor representations to composite load models and emerging power-electronic load models such as LDEV1 and PERC1. Measurement-based and component-based modeling approaches are reviewed along with their advantages, limitations, and validation requirements. The paper further discusses the role of large load models in power flow studies, voltage and transient stability assessments, electromagnetic transient simulations, and planning under uncertainty. Current utility practices, industry initiatives, and evolving interconnection requirements are also summarized. Finally, key challenges are identified, including model validation, data availability, platform inconsistencies, and the representation of converter-dominated loads. The review highlights the need for standardized modeling frameworks, improved measurement-based validation, and enhanced collaboration among utilities, researchers, and regulators to support the reliable integration of large loads into future power systems.

paper_title: IoT and Blockchain Applications in Agriculture: A Systematic Review of Techniques, Effectiveness, and Challenges
paper_abstract: Agriculture faces resource scarcity, climate variability and weak supply-chain transparency, and research on the Internet of Things (IoT) and blockchain as responses is fragmented. We conducted a systematic review reported under PRISMA 2020 of 79 sources (2012–2026; 58 from an initial search and 21 from a targeted 2024–2026 update). Sources were separated into 45 reviews and surveys, used as related work, and 34 regular research papers, of which 27 technical studies were coded by technique, components and application domain. IoT-based approaches account for 52% of the technical studies, integrated IoT–blockchain approaches for 26% and blockchain-only approaches for 19%; the integrated share rose from 10% in the initial search to 26% after the update. Crop applications make up 41% of studies and livestock-only applications 15%. Reported benefits include better monitoring, input efficiency, traceability and data trust, but effectiveness metrics are heterogeneous. An analytical model of sensing load, ledger throughput, Byzantine fault tolerance and sharding explains why integration stresses throughput. Scalability, interoperability, cost and digital skills remain barriers; lightweight and sharded consensus and field-validated integrated systems are priority directions.
