paper_title: Governed Memory for Autonomous Agents A Critical Review of Provenance Temporal Validity and Access
paper_abstract: Autonomous language-model agents need more than a searchable document collection. They must preserve observations, distinguish facts from inferences, update changing information, and construct a useful context under access and resource constraints. This review examines the database requirements created by those activities. It uses AI-native database as a functional design term for a data service supporting the agent memory lifecycle rather than as an established product category. A purposive narrative synthesis connects information retrieval, vector indexing, retrieval-augmented generation, agent memory, transaction isolation, and data provenance. The central contribution is a separation of authoritative records, append-only episodes, derived memories, and transient model context. A proposed record schema and retrieval workflow make provenance, temporal validity, authorization, and derivation explicit. The analysis explains why semantic similarity is insufficient for truth, why longer context does not replace memory management, and why deleting a source requires attention to derived summaries and embeddings. A hypothetical customer-support case illustrates conflict resolution and safe updates. A proposed mutation-sequence fixture links temporal validity, correction, derivative invalidation, and access enforcement to observable failures. No new database implementation or benchmark result is reported. The review argues that useful agent memory depends on controlled transformation and maintenance of evidence, not merely on retaining more tokens or selecting a particular storage engine.

paper_title: Efficient On-Policy Distillation for Language Models: A Survey of Costs, Trade-Offs, and Evaluation
paper_abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers teacher behavior through feedback on student-generated trajectories. Its efficiency is often expressed in incompatible units: fewer examples, shorter rollouts, lower memory, higher throughput, or cheaper deployment. These gains need not coincide, and an inexpensive update need not minimize the cost of reaching a target capability. We survey efficient OPD through six connected tracks: data, rollout, teacher supervision, optimization, systems, and deployment amortization. A common accounting framework separates additive resource expenditure from elapsed time and peak memory, while preserving differences in state distributions, teacher access, and learning objectives. We accompany the synthesis with a versioned evidence ledger that records the workload, denominator, measurement boundary, and quality condition behind reported efficiency results. The resulting audit exposes several sources of non-comparability, including changed sequence caps, omitted preparation, stage-local memory statistics, and increased scoring cost hidden by faster generation. Building on existing general and formula-driven OPD surveys, our contribution is an operational organization of efficiency evidence and a reproducible cost-to-quality evaluation protocol. We conclude with testable research questions about budget allocation, state coverage, supervision value, and amortized deployment. The literature cutoff is October 25, 2026; no new model-training experiments are claimed.

paper_title: One Marker, Many Circuits: A Scoping Review of Lactate Across Donor, Perfusate and Recipient Phases in Solid Organ Transplantation
paper_abstract: Objective: To map how lactate has been measured, interpreted and validated as a graft viability or outcome marker across donor, perfusate and recipient phases and organs. Background: Lactate is measured at every step of solid organ transplantation, but its meaning differs by phase, preservation method and organ. No review has mapped this evidence across the transplant continuum. Methods: Scoping review following JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science and CENTRAL were searched from 2000, supplemented by journal-targeted searches, citation chasing and ClinicalTrials.gov. Human clinical and ex vivo studies reporting lactate against graft viability or outcome were charted and mapped by organ and phase. Results: 159 human studies were included. Liver transplantation accounted for 108, mainly in the recipient phase and machine perfusion; heart contributed 28, lung 12, kidney 7 and pancreas 1, and no intestine study was eligible. Proposed liver perfusion thresholds ranged from below 1.7 to 4.1 mmol/L. In the largest cohort, lactate clearance did not predict graft survival (AUC 0.50). Day-1 lactate contributed to a validated primary nonfunction model (AUROC 0.83). Confounders included stored red cells in circuits, absence of a clearing organ, donor type, measurement timing and drugs. Conclusions: Lactate is a useful but organ- and context-dependent signal, strongest as a recipient-phase marker after liver transplantation and weakest as a stand-alone ex situ viability criterion outside the liver. Phase-specific thresholds, standardized reporting and multi-marker validation are needed before lactate is used to discard organs.

paper_title: Density Peak Clustering: A Systematic Survey of Methods, Applications, Challenges, and Future Research Directions
paper_abstract: Density Peak Clustering (DPC) is a widely studied unsupervised clustering method that identifies cluster centers using local density and relative separation without iterative prototype updates. Its simple and intuitive formulation has motivated extensive research, but its performance remains sensitive to data representation, distance measures, neighborhood construction, density estimation, center selection, assignment strategies, and data scale. To provide an updated and structured view of the field, this paper presents a systematic mapping review of DPC research published from 2014 to 8 August 2026. The survey first establishes the fundamental concepts, original DPC procedure, methodological evolution, and current methodological landscape. It then examines major application areas, including healthcare, cybersecurity, industrial monitoring, remote sensing and image analysis, transportation, networks, text analysis, multivariate time series, and scientific data. Subsequently, the methodological advances enabling modern DPC are organized into eight families: adaptive neighborhood and density estimation; graph, manifold, and multi-peak modeling; automatic center and cluster-number determination; assignment, merging, and uncertainty handling; representation learning; privacy-preserving, federated, and incremental computation; scalable execution; and auxiliary strategies such as sampling, grids, optimization, and limited supervision. Each methodological family is related to the limitation it addresses and the assumptions or computational costs it introduces. Finally, the survey synthesizes key lessons, research potential, persistent challenges, and future directions toward robust, interpretable, fairness-aware, privacy-preserving, reproducible, resource-efficient, uncertainty-aware, and continually adaptive DPC systems.

paper_title: From Algorithms to Bitstreams: A Survey of FPGA-Based Acceleration for Transformer Inference
paper_abstract: FPGA acceleration of Transformer inference involves model transformation, arithmetic optimization, memory organization, and deployment. This survey critically synthesizes 266 publications (2021–2026), identifying five mechanisms underlying performance gains: computation reduction, data movement reduction, arithmetic density, hardware utilization, and computational capacity. Quantization emerges as a frequently reported optimization, while architectural rankings depend on study selection and classification. Configuration-level comparisons and break-even analyses reveal how conversion, communication, integration overhead, and model quality constrain reported benefits. Supported by a traceable evidence map, the survey identifies limitations in existing evaluations and provides practical design guidance and controlled experiments for future FPGA-based Transformer accelerators.

paper_title: Feline Leukemia Virus and Feline Immunodeficiency Virus in Domestic and Free-Roaming Cats: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of North American Prevalence, Risk Factors, and Diagnostic Considerations, 1987–2024
paper_abstract: Feline leukemia virus (FeLV) and feline immunodeficiency virus (FIV) are important retroviral pathogens affecting domestic and free-roaming cats worldwide. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized prevalence, risk factors, diagnostic considerations, and epidemiological trends in North America from 1987 to 2024. Following the PRISMA framework, studies from the United States and Canada were evaluated using data from 285,080 cats for FIV and 183,296 cats for FeLV. Pooled prevalence was 4.02% (95% CI: 3.60–4.49%) for FIV and 3.57% (95% CI: 3.13–4.07%) for FeLV, with substantial heterogeneity among studies. Older age, male sex, intact male status, outdoor access, poor health, and feral or shelter status were associated with increased infection prevalence. Prevalence remained relatively stable overall but varied geographically and across population types. Diagnostic limitations, particularly detection of regressive FeLV infection, may influence prevalence estimates. These findings support integrated surveillance, improved diagnostic strategies, vaccination, and targeted population management.

paper_title: Comparative Efficacy and Tolerability of Herbal Versus Pharmaceutical Antidepressants in Adults with Depression: A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: Background: Depression is a major cause of disability worldwide. Pharmaceutical antidepressants are standard treatments for moderate to severe depression; however, adverse effects, tolerability concerns, and incomplete treatment responses have increased interest in herbal alternatives. Evidence directly comparing herbal and pharmaceutical antidepressants remains inconsistent. Objective: To examine and synthesise evidence on the comparative efficacy, safety, and tolerability of herbal versus pharmaceutical antidepressants in adults with depression. Methods: A scoping review was conducted using MEDLINE, EMBASE, PsycINFO, AMED, CENTRAL, and grey literature sources. Eligible studies were primary comparative clinical studies involving adults aged 18 years and older with depressive disorders or clinically significant depressive symptoms. Data were synthesised according to Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Results: Twenty-one comparative studies met the inclusion criteria. Hypericum perforatum (St John’s wort) was the most frequently investigated herbal intervention, while selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, serotonin–norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, and tricyclic antidepressants were the main pharmaceutical comparators. Standardised Hypericum perforatum preparations demonstrated efficacy comparable to selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors in mild to moderate depression. Pharmaceutical antidepressants, however, showed more consistent benefits in moderate to severe depression. Herbal interventions were generally associated with fewer adverse effects and lower treatment discontinuation rates. Conclusion: Herbal antidepressants, particularly standardised Hypericum perforatum preparations, may offer an effective and better-tolerated treatment option for some adults with mild to moderate depression. However, variations in study design, intervention standardisation, and reporting limit definitive conclusions. Further high-quality comparative research is required to strengthen the evidence base and guide clinical decision-making and support evidence-based treatment recommendations. What this study adds: This review highlights the severity-dependent efficacy and tolerability of pharmaceutical and natural antidepressants. Standardized Hypericum perforatum is identified as a potentially useful and better-tolerated treatment for mild-to-moderate depression, but it also highlights safety issues, especially herb–drug interactions, and important data gaps that need to be studied.

paper_title: Lung Transplantation in Mounier-Kuhn Syndrome: Successful Consecutive Cases and Review of the Literature
paper_abstract: Background: Mounier-Kuhn syndrome is a rare disorder characterized by marked dilatation of the trachea and main bronchi, respiratory infections, bronchiectasis, and progressive respiratory failure. Lung transplantation (LTx) in this condition has only rarely been reported and may be technically challenging because of the abnormal size and structure of the main airways. Case presentation: We describe two consecutive patients with Mounier-Kuhn syndrome who underwent bilateral lung transplantation at our center. Both patients had advanced respiratory disease with marked tracheobronchial dilatation. In the first patient, preoperative planning included patient-specific three-dimensional reconstruction and printing of the trachea and proximal bronchi. Because of severe enlargement of the recipient bronchus, a telescopic bronchial anastomosis was used. The postoperative course was complicated by bronchial stenosis requiring repeated bronchoscopic interventions and stent placement. The second patient underwent bilateral LTx without major airway complications and had a favorable early postoperative course. Conclusions: Lung transplantation can be successfully performed in selected patients with end-stage respiratory failure due to Mounier-Kuhn syndrome. Careful preoperative airway assessment and individualized planning of bronchial anastomosis are crucial in such patients.

paper_title: Geriatric Medicine in Ethiopia: A Narrative Review of Physician Training Gaps and Interdisciplinary Team Establishment
paper_abstract: Background: Geriatric Medicine is a medical specialty concerned with the health and wellbeing of older adults. Despite the rapid increase in the geriatric population in Ethiopia, the access to specialized care among older patients is limited. There are significant gaps in integrating geriatric competencies across the medical curriculum and the interdisciplinary team for geriatric medicine in Ethiopia. Methods: A narrative review was conducted via PubMed and Google Scholar to identify studies on Geriatric Medicine in Ethiopia. The literature search was supplemented by targeted web searches and reference snowballing. Results: No directly related literature was identified during the initial search. Furthermore, implementation of the Geriatrics framework in Ethiopia is critically limited by a severe lack of specialized training and curricula. This lack of knowledge leads to various clinical misdiagnoses and service gaps. On the other hand, an international academic partnership in 2024 successfully initiated the integration of core geriatric topics into medical training. Conclusion: Strengthening the geriatric workforce requires formal recognition, structured training, and the active integration of multidisciplinary care teams across Ethiopia.

paper_title: Labisia pumila (Kacip Fatimah) Extracts: Aligning Extraction Research with the Clinical, Regulatory and Safety Evidence—A Critical Review
paper_abstract: Extraction studies of Labisia pumila (kacip fatimah) usually select solvents by yield, phenolic acid content and antioxidant assays. A representative study recommended supercritical carbon dioxide with 70% ethanol–water co-solvent for the leaves of var. pumila. This review asks whether such optimisation produces extracts comparable to those with human, regulatory or safety evidence. The only placebo-controlled trial of a single-herb extract used a water extract of var. alata, and the extract assessed by the European Food Safety Authority was a hydroalcoholic extract of the whole plant, judged safe only up to 350 mg/day. Recalculation from the source study shows that its three phenolic markers made up at most 1.7% of any extract and that the best supercritical extract contained about one-twelfth of the maximum gallic acid content specified for the EFSA-assessed material. The superiority of supercritical extraction over maceration was confounded by temperature and solvent volume. The CO2-only extract, discarded for lacking phenolic acids, is the fraction most likely to contain the alkylresorcinols identified as oestrogen receptor ligands. Labisia pumila extracts should be specified by variety, plant part, solvent and mechanism-relevant markers, and optimised against a clinically tested reference rather than generic antioxidant assays.

paper_title: Where the Harness Meets the Physical World: A Survey of the Physical Agentic Harness
paper_abstract: Embodied foundation models now allow robots to act on open-ended instructions, yet success on long-horizon physical tasks also depends on the runtime around the model, which organizes the task, invokes skills, guards execution, and retains experience. Digital agent research treats this runtime, known as the harness, as a first-class design object that can be engineered and even improved from experience, since the same model can perform very differently under different harnesses. Such harness designs do not carry over directly, because physical execution is embodiment-specific, partially observed, time-constrained, and often irreversible, which also makes experience costly to learn from. Embodied AI systems increasingly build similar runtimes, yet the field still lacks a unified view of them. This survey treats the physical agentic harness as a research object in its own right. We define it as the runtime system that maintains task and execution state for an embodied foundation model and mediates the model’s interaction with the physical world through one or more physical bodies. We then review over 200 works and organize them by six functional responsibilities: task orchestration, digital resources, embodied capabilities, execution governance, digital-physical interaction, and persistent evolution. This organization offers a common lens for comparing methods across communities, making explicit how model decisions reach physical execution and how grounded evidence flows back. The reviewed benchmarks and applications provide limited evidence of individual runtime contributions, particularly the effects of execution governance and sustained gains from persistent evolution. We close with open problems in model-harness co-design, capability composition, real-time decision making, distributed execution, and continual improvement from physical experience.

paper_title: ApoE4 and Psychosis in Neurodegenerative and Non-Neurodegenerative Disease: A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: Psychosis is a neuropsychiatric feature found across neurodegenerative conditions including Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and Parkinson’s disease (PD). It is also a common feature in psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia. The apolipoprotein E epsilon 4 (ApoE4) allele is an established genetic risk factor for AD that may also increase the risk of psychosis. However, evidence regarding the association between ApoE4 and psychosis remains unclear. This paper evaluates the relationship between "ApoE" 4 carrier status and psychosis in both neurodegenerative (Alzheimer’s disease and Parkinson’s disease) and non-neurodegenerative disorders (schizophrenia). Additionally it explores whether sex and zygosity modulate this association.A literature review of studies identified through PubMed and Scopus was conducted. Thirty- one studies, were included that investigated the relationship between ApoE4 and psychosis in select neurodegenerative and psychiatric populations. Studies were included if they assessed ApoE4 status in relation to the presence, severity, or age of onset of psychosis.Among the 16 AD- focused studies, a positive association was reported in 11 while 4 showed no significant association and one showed an inverse correlation. ApoE4 carriers and ApoE4 homozygotes that were female were reported to have the strongest association. The three studies examining PD resulted in inconsistent findings limited by small sample sizes. With respect to schizophrenia, associations were predominantly null or inconsistent. There was limited evidence for the influence of sex or ApoE4 zygosity.Of note the risk was enhanced in female carriers and "ApoE" 4 homozygotes. In terms of PD results were conflicting, limited by small sample sizes. Schizophrenia studies produced findings that were predominantly null or equivocal, with no clear evidence that sex or zygosity influenced outcomes.ApoE4 positivity appears to have a stronger association with psychosis in AD compared to PD or schizophrenia. Available evidence suggests that this relationship may be modified by sex and ApoE4 zygosity and that female ApoE4 homozygotes are particularly vulnerable. Findings were however limited by substantial heterogeneity across studies and limited evidence in PD and schizophrenia populations. Thus larger studies are needed to clarify the role of ApoE4 in psychosis, particularly in non-AD cohorts.

paper_title: Accountable Enterprise Agents A Critical Review of Authorization Execution and Recovery
paper_abstract: Enterprise agents combine language models, persistent state, and executable tools to pursue goals across business systems. Their practical significance lies in the transition from generating information to changing organizational state. This critical review examines authorization, execution, and recovery at that transition and develops disconfirmable tests of the proposed controls. A purposively selected literature corpus links reasoning and tool-use methods with agent benchmarks, retrieval and memory research, security studies, and organizational risk guidance. The review is interpretive rather than systematic and does not report new experiments. Its central argument is that execution authority should be separated from model-generated plans. A reference architecture is developed around authenticated task intake, evidence retrieval, bounded planning, external policy enforcement, transactional execution, and independent outcome verification. The architecture is applied to a hypothetical procurement workflow to show why correct language output, valid API calls, and authorized business outcomes are different properties. The synthesis identifies coupled failures involving stale evidence, ambiguous delegation, repeated execution, and incomplete recovery. It proposes an evaluation framework covering task completion, policy adherence, repeatability, recovery, human workload, and cost per verified outcome. Future research should test controls under policy changes, asynchronous failures, and organizational handoffs rather than assume that benchmark success establishes production readiness. Enterprise agent design is best understood as the design of accountable execution systems in which language models propose actions within explicitly constrained authority.

paper_title: Visual Generative AI for Extended Reality: A Survey
paper_abstract: Visual generative models create objects, spatial scenes, time-varying 3D content, and action-conditioned observations for extended reality (XR). Using these outputs requires knowing which viewing, editing, and state-changing operations they support, and which system components supply those operations. This critical narrative review catalogues 204 methods and systems and traces generated outputs into specific XR operations. Four comparison axes organize content units, generative mechanisms, representations, and operating stages; common mathematical definitions clarify conditioning and update rules. An evidence map records eight capability dimensions for a purposively selected subset of 31 methods and systems. The synthesis combines these profiles with source-specific quantitative comparisons and deployment studies, identifying the components, configurations, and endpoints supporting capability claims. Building on paradigm-level comparisons, this analysis distinguishes the evidence needed to generate editable structure, preserve an accepted modification, and respond to tracked input. Visual recall and modification retention require different references, while generation throughput and input-to-display latency describe different parts of the response path. Worked task comparisons explain how these distinctions change the choice between prepared geometry with local rendering and continuing observation generation. We derive task-specific selection criteria and propose matched evaluations of binocular viewing, preview replacement, persistent changes, response scheduling, and physical-space alignment. The resulting framework connects model selection to explicit task requirements and identifies the additional tests needed to assess XR use. The survey homepage is available at https://edhuang1.github.io/xr-survey/.

paper_title: Bayesian Inference of Expensive Simulators: Survey and Comparison of Design Choices
paper_abstract: We present a survey of approaches to Bayesian inference with simulator forward models, focusing on settings with prohibitively expensive simulators. In this domain, Bayesian optimization-based methods have emerged as the most promising approach. We unify existing methods into a general framework, enabling consistent reasoning about shared algorithmic structure across the fragmented literature. Within this framework, we identify the primary design choices and perform a systematic empirical comparison of their effects on inference efficiency in terms of required simulation budget.   A key result of our study is that inference efficiency is often dominated by the choice of surrogate-model response variable, as it directly governs the complexity of the modeled function. Specifically, we demonstrate that the prevalent scalar log-likelihood is a poor response variable, as it discards crucial information. Based on this insight, we introduce the concept of custom \emph{proxy variables}: transformations of simulator outputs engineered to retain more information and provide smoother response surfaces, substantially improving inference efficiency over standard response variables.   We provide actionable guidance and a numerically robust Julia package to facilitate practical adoption of Bayesian optimization for simulator inverse problems.
comments: 25 pages, 8 figures. Accepted for publication in Statistics and Computing. This is the submitted manuscript; the revised version, including changes based on peer review, is available from the authors upon request

paper_title: Dependency Graphs of Mathematical Arguments: Representation, Structural Measurement, and Proof Review
paper_abstract: We propose a source-grounded framework for representing and measuring mathematical arguments with assistance from large language models. It includes numbered and unnumbered statements, equations, assumptions, and constructions, distinguishing source occurrences from contextual states and inference records. Proposed dependencies retain source evidence and review status. A measurement contract fixes manuscript versions, boundaries, granularity, proof choices, and macro anchors. On a selected finite directed acyclic graph, depth is the longest prerequisite-path length, and bulk counts distinct ancestor edges. We give a union recurrence that accounts for shared subarguments and identify reachability conditions preserving depth and the macro skeleton; unrestricted refinement need not preserve depth or bulk. A standardized, versioned prompt protocol separates annotation discovery, deterministic recomputation, and review assistance. Cross-paper links support a research agenda on theorem co-use, rare combinations, and connections between dependency communities. These patterns motivate probabilistic premise suggestions and review of possible omissions or unchecked application conditions in human-written and AI-generated proofs. Further applications include source-linked reading support and comparison of individual and collaborative argument shapes. We provide an evaluation design rather than empirical evidence of these benefits. Suggested premises require mathematical validation, and the measures describe a specified representation rather than intrinsic mathematical difficulty, originality, or importance.

paper_title: FilingLoop: Evaluating and Evolving LLM Agents for Corporate Disclosure Review and Revision
paper_abstract: Public disclosure repositories such as SEC EDGAR support informed investment through web access to corporate filings. Supporting their review with language model agents requires discovering unstated deficiencies across related documents, acquiring missing company facts, and verifying that requested revisions satisfy evidence-backed requirements. Existing financial question-answering evaluations provide limited evidence of these interactive capabilities. We introduce \textbf{FilingLoop}, an interactive benchmark and a self-evolving agent framework for corporate disclosure review and revision. Grounded in historical U.S.\ Securities and Exchange Commission correspondence, FilingLoop reconstructs 380 predominantly IPO review tasks from 96 companies under distinct information constraints. An evaluator separate from the acting agents scores final filings and responses against 6,099 eligible requirements and audits unsupported claims and harmful revisions. Our framework couples iterative review and revision within each case with procedural learning across cases, converting requirement-level evaluation feedback into role-specific guidance without updating model weights. Updates affect only subsequent cases, allowing procedural adaptation to be assessed without retrying scored tasks. On the evaluated stream, evolution increases requirement fulfillment from 24.28\% to 27.96\% and full comment resolution from 16.90\% to 20.75\%, with a 5.8\% increase in total cost over the fixed-policy variant. FilingLoop connects the concerns an agent discovers with the company facts it obtains and the revisions it commits, providing requirement-level feedback for procedures used in later review tasks.

paper_title: Medicinal Plants with Neuroprotective Potential in Neurodegenerative Diseases: A Critical Review of Phytochemistry, Mechanisms and Evidence, with Relevance to Bangladesh
paper_abstract: Many plants used traditionally to aid memory have been put forward as neuroprotective candidates against dementia. This mini review weighs the preclinical and clinical evidence for six of them (Centella asiatica, Ginkgo biloba, Salvia species, Withania somnifera, Bacopa monnieri and Semecarpus anacardium), briefly describes five more, and considers their relevance to Bangladesh. Sources were PubMed, Google Scholar and Semantic Scholar, with a targeted update in 2026. In cells and rodents, the same mechanisms recur cholinergic modulation, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity, and protection against amyloid-beta toxicity. Human evidence is thin. Two large ginkgo trials did not prevent dementia, while small trials of sage, ashwagandha and Bacopa point to modest cognitive gains. Centella and Semecarpus have no controlled human data. Before any clinical recommendation, the field needs standardised extracts, safety assessment, and adequately powered trials in people at the earliest stages of Alzheimer's disease.

paper_title: Securing Multilingual Legal Information Infrastructures: A Systematic Mapping Review and Threat-and-Failure-Mode Taxonomy for Terminological Integrity
paper_abstract: Multilingual legal information infrastructures connect official legislation repositories, terminology databases, translation memories, ontologies, search services, and artificial-intelligence systems. Conventional confidentiality-integrity-availability controls do not fully address a distinctive failure: a technically unchanged record can convey the wrong legal concept because its source, version, concept identity, cross-language scope, semantic relation, or approval history is defective. This article presents a PRISMA-informed systematic mapping review and standards synthesis. Ten query clusters yielded 100 retained scholarly occurrences and 41 official-document occurrences; after deduplication and screening, 52 substantive scholarly sources and 30 current standards, specifications, legal instruments, and guidance documents were included, with four methodology sources analysed separately. Of the scholarly corpus, 53.8% was empirical or technical, 38.5% conceptual or doctrinal, and 7.7% review-based; only 25.0% directly examined multilingual legal systems and 7.7% explicitly addressed low-resource languages. Evidence concentrated on semantic corruption, poisoning of data and retrieval, and governance/privacy, while script-specific attacks remained thinly studied. The review develops MLTIT, a seven-family taxonomy containing 33 threat and failure modes; MLTIAF, a fifteen-control defence-in-depth architecture; and a seven-risk privacy layer mapped to NIST, ISO, OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, Unicode, and legal-document standards. Analytical application to four observed Kazakh-Russian terminology discrepancies and one negative control in the SOZZ online dictionary illustrates the model’s discriminating function without treating the records as a prevalence sample or evidence of malicious attack. The central design rule is that AI may detect, rank, and explain risk, but may not autonomously alter authoritative legal content.

paper_title: State Legitimacy, Governance Failures and the Rise of Vigilantism in South Africa: A Systematic Review of Political Patronage, Law Enforcement and Militia-Like Group Emergence
paper_abstract: Introduction: Vigilantism in South Africa is associated in the supplied literature with frustration over crime, slow or ineffective justice, inadequate policing, corruption, political interference and weakened public trust. However, the evidence is heterogeneous and direct evidence concerning the organisation, political sponsorship and proliferation of militia-like groups remains limited and is still confined in the pre-democratic South Africa era. Methods: The researcher-selected databases and information sources were Google Scholar, ERIC. The eligibility protocol restricted publication years to 2020–2026. COSTAQDA recorded source-level retrieval through OpenAlex (250 retrieved; 3049 available), Crossref (250 retrieved; 17170 available). Where researcher-selected sources did not expose a suitable direct bulk-search connector, COSTAQDA used its OpenAlex/Crossref discovery bridge while preserving the researcher-selected source names in the PRISMA record. The identification run recorded 500 records before cross-source deduplication and 498 unique records after deduplication. Results: Seven codes were developed into three categories and four analytical themes. Vigilantism was associated with perceived unavailability or ineffectiveness of formal protection; legitimacy was weakened by both non-performance and coercive or corrupt performance; community enforcement was valued for immediacy but remained dangerous and contested; and lawful community-policing institutions represented a possible alternative. Direct evidence linking political patronage to organised militia formation was thin. Discussion/Conclusion: The evidence supports an association between institutional failure, weakened legitimacy and community resort to extra-legal enforcement, but does not establish a single causal pathway or demonstrate that political patronage independently produces militia-like groups.

paper_title: A Review of Optical Fibre Sensors Operating in the Visible Region: Fundamentals, Technological Developments and Biomedical Applications
paper_abstract: Optical fiber sensors have experienced remarkable development due to their advantages in sensitivity, immunity to electromagnetic interference, compact size, and remote monitoring capability. Among them, devices operating in the visible spectral region have gained particular attention because of their low cost, ease of implementation, and potential for biomedical, chemical, and environmental applications. This review presents the fundamentals and recent advances in visible-light-based optical fiber sensors, covering the main interferometric configurations, including Michelson, Mach–Zehnder, Fabry–Pérot, and Sagnac interferometers. In addition, different sensing platforms, such as single-mode, multimode, plastic, and photonic optical fibers, are analyzed, highlighting their characteristics and advantages for specific applications. Various sensing mechanisms are reviewed, including optical absorption, fluorescence, surface plasmon resonance, and evanescent field sensing. Furthermore, applications focused on the measurement of pH, glucose, pressure, humidity, and other parameters of biomedical and environmental interest are discussed. The studies analyzed demonstrate that the combination of optical fibers with functional materials and spectroscopic techniques in the visible region enables the development of highly sensitive, selective, and real-time monitoring sensors. Finally, the current challenges and future perspectives of this technology for scientific and industrial applications are presented.

paper_title: Analgesic Management of Robot-Assisted Surgery for Mediastinal Tumors: A Review of Pain Mechanisms, Regional Anesthesia, and Multimodal Analgesia
paper_abstract: Background: Robot-assisted thoracic surgery (RATS) for mediastinal tumors is a minimally invasive approach that offers three-dimensional magnified visualization, tremor filtration, and articulated instruments. Although it is expected to reduce postoperative pain compared with open surgery, pain may still arise from intercostal ports, subxiphoid incisions and chest tubes. Therefore, a consistent multimodal analgesic strategy is needed from the intraoperative to the postoperative period, tailored to the surgical approach and port placement. Objective: This review aims to characterize the mechanisms underlying postoperative pain after RATS for mediastinal tumors and to examine the current evidence and clinical indications for systemic analgesics and regional analgesic techniques, including thoracic epidural analgesia (TEA), peripheral nerve blocks, and local wound infiltration. Conclusions: Routine use of TEA may not be necessary for all patients undergoing RATS for medi-astinal tumors. In most cases, a multimodal analgesic regimen based on acetaminophen, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, or cyclooxygenase-2 selective inhibitors, supplemented with a single-shot regional block or local wound infiltration according to the surgical approach and port placement, appears reasonable. However, individualized analgesic strategies incorporating continuous regional analgesia should be considered in patients undergoing extensive thymectomy, those requiring ports across multiple intercostal spaces, those at risk of conversion to open surgery, and those with severe preoperative pain or an increased risk of chronic postoperative pain.

paper_title: Exploring the Lived Experiences of South African Widows in Relation to Work and Family Within a Cultural Context: A Systematic Review
paper_abstract: Introduction: Widowhood in South African and related African contexts is shaped by mourning obligations, gendered authority, inheritance insecurity, economic responsibility and culturally specific expectations. However, the relationship between these conditions and widows’ navigation of work and family life remains insufficiently understood. This systematic review examined how South African widows experience and navigate the intersection of work and family within sociocultural and traditional contexts, including challenges, opportunities, coping strategies, enabling conditions and.Methods: The researcher-selected databases and information sources were ERIC, PubMed (MEDLINE) and Google Scholar. The eligibility protocol restricted publication years to 2015–2026. The exact calendar date of search execution was not recorded in the verified identification provenance; this is distinct from the publication-year eligibility range. ERIC, PubMed (MEDLINE) and Google Scholar were searched using a specified Boolean strategy for English-language peer-reviewed studies published from 2015 to 2026.Results: The synthesis identified four themes: widowhood is socially regulated through gendered cultural expectations; economic survival links work, family responsibility and wellbeing; agency is exercised through rights negotiation and collective resistance; and support needs to be culturally responsive and practically accessible. Rituals could restrict autonomy and participation, but culturally grounded ritual could also be experienced as empowering. Direct evidence on how South African widows combine paid work, unpaid care, household duties and cultural obligations was sparse. Work-family evidence from general South African employee populations was contextual rather than widow-specific.Discussion/Conclusion: South African widows navigate work and family through an interaction of cultural regulation, economic pressure, institutional constraint and individual or collective agency. Effective responses should protect rights, strengthen economic and psychosocial support, and remain culturally responsive.

paper_title: Large Video Generative Models: A Systematic Survey
paper_abstract: Video generation has wide applications in cinematic production, autonomous systems, interactive entertainment, and domain-specific content creation. In the last couple of years, we have witnessed remarkable progress in video generation technologies, largely driven by large video generative models (LVGMs), which enable the generation of long and high-quality videos. In comparison to traditional video generative models, LVGMs are trained on much more data, have substantially more parameters, and have much stronger zero-shot capabilities on a wide range of video generation tasks. The exciting advances and new challenges in this area call for a systematic analysis on the core technologies and insights. Towards this end, we provide a systematic survey on LVGMs. We first provide a formal definition of LVGMs, and then cover the core technical components including model architectures, data construction, training and evaluation. Finally, we discuss the applications and future directions of LVGMs. This survey serves as a guide for understanding the mechanisms of LVGMs and building them.

paper_title: Mechanistic Interpretability of LLM Behavior: A Survey
paper_abstract: Mechanistic interpretability seeks to explain how internal computations produce large language model behaviors, yet findings remain fragmented across methods and behavioral domains. We survey 229 papers across five behavior families: epistemic, linguistic, reasoning, safety, and social behaviors. We introduce a framework distinguishing five levels of mechanistic evidence, from decodability to generalization. Our cross-behavior synthesis reveals recurring mechanisms, distinctions between representation and causal control, and limitations of existing explanations. We conclude by identifying gaps in understanding computational roles, behavioral interactions, and generalization to interactive and agentic settings.

paper_title: Structured Clinical Communication in Multidisciplinary Surgical Teams: A Narrative Review of SBAR, TeamSTEPPS, and Physician–Nurse Collaboration
paper_abstract: Background/Objectives: Reliable physician–nurse communication is essential throughout the perioperative pathway, yet information exchange may be compromised by hierarchy, fragmented workflows, and unclear responsibilities. This narrative review critically examines evidence on SBAR and TeamSTEPPS in multidisciplinary surgical teams, emphasizing nursing leadership, implementation, and the distinction between communication improvements and patient outcomes. Methods: Targeted PubMed searches and supplementary scholarly web searches, updated on 8 September 2026, informed purposive selection of empirical studies, existing reviews, methodological publications, and institutional guidance. Surgical and perioperative evidence was prioritized; findings from other settings were considered for their contextual relevance. Manuscript preparation was informed by SANRA. Evidence was synthesized qualitatively, considering study design, implementation fidelity, professional participation, outcome measurement, and sustainability. Results: Structured communication interventions generally favored information completeness, staff perceptions, and selected teamwork behaviors. Evidence for sustained reductions in postoperative morbidity or mortality was less consistent and frequently derived from uncontrolled or multicomponent interventions. SBAR implementation fidelity varied, while Team-STEPPS outcomes depended on local adaptation, reinforcement, and professional engagement. Hierarchical relationships, workload, and limited opportunities to speak up complicated implementation. The synthesis informed a conceptual surgical framework linking SBAR, an established TeamSTEPPS component, with reciprocal acknowledgement, agreed action, identified responsibility, and feedback. This framework has not undergone empirical validation. Conclusions: Structured communication in surgical care requires organizational support that enables information to prompt coordinated clinical action. Nursing leadership and active medical participation are central implementation considerations. Prospective evaluation should distinguish implementation fidelity, observed collaborative behaviors, care processes, and patient outcomes, while assessing workload and sustainability.

paper_title: Longwall Top-Coal Caving: A Review of Geomechanics, Recovery, Operational Control, and Technology
paper_abstract: Longwall top-coal caving (LTCC) combines the mechanical extraction of the lower seam with caving and drawing of the coal above the cutting horizon. Its performance depends on linked geomechanical, strata-support, granular-flow, operational, and control processes: caving does not by itself ensure selective recovery. This global critical review synthesises research on stress redistribution, fracture-controlled cavability, roof rupture and weighting, drawbody and coal–gangue boundary evolution, drawing interval and sequence, support interaction, hazards, modelling, monitoring, and automation. It distinguishes recurring mechanisms from mine-specific numerical settings and appraises the evidence by study type, represented variables, and degree of field validation. The review's central contribution is a mechanism-to-control assurance framework that connects potential failure states to candidate indicators, mine-approved responses, and verification measures. It treats drawing initiation, sequence, adjustment, and termination as safety-critical decisions within a multi-objective goal of clean-coal recovery, dilution control, ground stability, and hazard management. The evidence remains dominated by simulations and mine-specific cases, with few end-to-end field-validated control demonstrations. The proposed framework is a synthesis for testing, not a validated universal controller; indicators and operating limits require site-specific calibration and field verification.

paper_title: Food Choice as a Dynamic Behaviour: An Integrative Narrative Review of Determinants, Theoretical Frameworks, and Behaviour-Change Approaches
paper_abstract: Food choice is a multidimensional behaviour shaped by interactions among biological, psychological, social, cultural, economic, and environmental determinants. Understanding how these influences combine is essential for explaining food choice and identifying barriers to healthier dietary behaviours. This narrative review synthesises literature identified through searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar and organises the determinants of food choice into food-related, individual, and socio-environmental domains. Food-related influences include sensory properties, palatability, and nutritional composition. Individual influences encompass appetite regulation, reward responses, emotions, nutrition knowledge, self-efficacy, habits, and learned experiences. Socio-environmental influences include household practices, cultural norms, affordability, accessibility, and marketing. The review also considers established behavioural theories, including the Theory of Planned Behaviour, the Health Belief Model, and Social Cognitive Theory, alongside behaviour-change approaches such as COM-B and nudge/choice architecture. The synthesis highlights how these domains may jointly facilitate or constrain healthier choices: nutrition knowledge may be limited by affordability and availability, emotional responses may interact with food reward and environmental exposure, and sensory acceptance may develop within family routines. Building on these relationships, the review links selected combinations of determinants to potential intervention priorities and specific research questions. Future research should distinguish stated preferences and intentions from observed purchasing and consumption and examine these relationships over time in everyday settings. This perspective can inform the development and evaluation of context-sensitive strategies for nutrition practice and public health.

paper_title: LLM-Based Agentic AI in Manufacturing: A Scoping Review of Applications, System Designs and Evaluation Practices
paper_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used in manufacturing to design products, plan production, diagnose faults and operate equipment, but their designs and evaluations remain difficult to compare. We analyse 164 studies identified through Scopus, Web of Science and IEEE Xplore to examine manufacturing applications, agentic system designs and evaluation practices, and to identify where evaluation coverage falls short of the evidence that these task and design types would require. We propose taxonomies of applications, agentic designs and evaluation practices, and relate task and design characteristics to the evidence required to assess them. The findings reveal an imbalance between assessing output quality and verifying whether outputs satisfy manufacturing requirements. For planning and decision-making systems, executability and constraint compliance receive limited evaluation, while most evidence comes from offline data or simulation. Limited assessment of safety, stability across repeated runs and performance in industrial settings leaves a gap between demonstrated task performance and evidence of reliable operation under manufacturing conditions. The resulting taxonomies and evidence requirements help researchers select evaluations suited to each manufacturing use case and distinguish demonstrated task performance from evidence of reliable operation.

paper_title: From Plan Generation to Reliable Execution: An Architecture-Centric Survey of Embodied Long-Horizon LLM Agents
paper_abstract: Long-horizon embodied agents employ large language models (LLMs) or vision-language models (VLMs) as cognitive cores to complete multi-stage tasks through sustained interaction. Their primary challenge is not to generate long plans, but to maintain task state under partial observability, environmental change, and delayed feedback, adapt actions to execution outcomes, and prevent local errors from propagating. Research is accordingly moving from plan generation and skill invocation toward state maintenance, execution verification, and failure recovery. Existing surveys, however, commonly organize the literature by foundation model or individual technique and thus provide limited insight into how these mechanisms jointly shape system behavior. We propose an architecture-level framework spanning planning, action interfaces, memory, execution feedback, world models, and multi-agent collaboration. A Method-by-Dimension Matrix compares module information flow, invocation conditions, and authority to modify behavior, and we assess whether current evaluations support architectural attribution. The evidence indicates that long-horizon capability depends less on plan length, memory capacity, or module count than on maintaining task- and environment-consistent state and ensuring that module outputs affect subsequent behavior when required. We synthesize the resulting trade-offs, open problems, and research directions to provide common coordinates for method comparison, architecture design, and evaluation.

paper_title: Liposomal Nanoformulations for Skin Delivery of Bioactive Botanical Extracts: A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: This article provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in liposomal nanoformulations encapsulating whole-plant extracts for topical skin applications, with a focus on research published between 2016 and 2026. Literature searches were conducted using the Web of Science, Scopus and PubMed databases. The evolution from conventional liposomes to advanced nanovesicles (ethosomes, transfersomes, transethosomes, propylene glycol- and glycerol-enriched liposomes, and (bio)polymer-coated nanovesicles) is analyzed alongside their integration into hybrid liposome-in-vehicle delivery systems. Liposome preparation methods, bilayer constituents, and semisolid vehicles used to increase viscosity of liquid liposomal dispersions were evaluated and discussed with respect to their physicochemical properties as well as the botanical, phytochemical and biological activity profiles and skin-related effects of the plant-extract-loaded liposomal nanocarriers. Encapsulation into liposomes was found to significantly enhance the stability of botanical extracts, their cutaneous deposition, as well as therapeutic efficacy and dermocosmetic potential. Reported biological effects were categorized according to their pharmacological activities, such as antioxidant, anti-melanogenic, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, cytotoxic, wound-healing, and anti-aging activities. In response to the growing demand for clean beauty and plant-based dermatological solutions, this article summarizes current knowledge on plant-extract-loaded liposomal nanoformulations to guide future research toward their potential applications in dermatology and cosmetology.

paper_title: Not Asked or Not Answered? Missingness Provenance in Youth Suicide-Attempt Prediction Using the Combined Youth Risk Behavior Survey, 2015–2023
paper_abstract: Pooled multi-site surveys mix several reasons a predictor can be absent: a jurisdiction did not ask the item, the item was not on that year’s questionnaire, or a student did not answer. Prediction models usually treat all of these as one missing value. Here, we use the CDC Youth Risk Behavior Survey combined high-school data, 2015–2023 (1,008,297 records; 250 site-year surveys), and code each predictor cell by provenance using only what the released data identify. Ten models predicted past-year suicide attempt (684,688 students) and injurious suicide attempt (504,707 students) from 15 behavioural items and demographics, comparing conventional handling (complete-case analysis, mean imputation, missing indicators, chained-equations imputation and gradient boosting) with provenance-aware indicators and pattern submodels. Evaluation used held-out school clusters, survey weights and a cluster bootstrap, and a structure-only model and 12 sensitivity analyses tested whether gains reflected survey recognition. Weighted prevalence was 8.8–10.7% for any attempt and 3.1–3.4% for injurious attempt. Most absent predictor cells came from surveys not asking the item (10.5% of all cells) rather than missingness where asked (3.5%). Provenance-split indicators improved AUROC over a single missing indicator by 0.0037 (95% CI 0.0019–0.0057) for any attempt and 0.0057 (0.0023–0.0090) for injurious attempt; the best model reached 0.853 and 0.849, whereas a site-year-and-pattern-only model reached 0.55. The gain disappeared in the national survey, where sites do not omit items, and grew when whole jurisdictions were held out (0.0054 and 0.0104). In a contrasting adult test bed built from BRFSS 2023 adverse childhood experience items, provenance handling made no difference. Distinguishing “not asked” from “not answered” gives small, consistent and transportable gains in pooled youth-survey prediction that are not explained by survey recognition, and pooled-survey analyses should code the source of absence.

paper_title: The Intellectual Genealogy of Education 6.0: A Critical Review of Pedagogical, Epistemic, and Technological Frameworks
paper_abstract: Education 6.0 has emerged as a conceptual orientation through which scholars explore the future of education in contexts shaped by artificial intelligence (AI), adaptive learning, human–machine collaboration, epistemic pluralism, and complex societal transformation. Yet the growing use of the label raises important questions concerning its intellectual genealogy, conceptual coherence, and relationship to earlier educational paradigms. This critical review examines selected publications from 2023 to 2026 to reconstruct the documented development of Education 6.0, distinguish its principal conceptual strands, and identify directions for theoretical and empirical research. Particular attention is given to Pitshou Moleka’s 2023 publications, including Dispelling the Limitations of Education 5.0 and Outlining the Vision of Education 6.0 and Exploring the Role of Artificial Intelligence in Education 6.0: Enhancing Personalized Learning and Adaptive Pedagogy. The review also considers subsequent contributions addressing AI-enabled personalization, human-centred educational technology, interdisciplinary learning, cultural knowledge, and ethical governance. It argues that Education 6.0 should not be treated as a universally standardized model but as an emerging and internally differentiated conceptual field. The review proposes a five-dimensional analytical framework encompassing pedagogical adaptability, human agency, ethical governance, epistemic pluralism, and systemic sustainability. This framework offers a basis for comparing competing formulations and designing empirical studies. The review identifies Moleka’s 2023 publications as documented early contributions to the conceptual development of Education 6.0, while recognizing that establishing exclusive intellectual priority would require a broader and reproducible examination of antecedent literature.

paper_title: Public Administration as an Enabling Architecture for the Sustainable Development Goals in Nigeria: An Integrative Review and Conceptual Framework
paper_abstract: Nigeria's progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) depends not only on the volume of resources committed to health, education, gender equality, infrastructure and peace, but on the administrative systems that convert policy into delivered services. This preprint presents an integrative review and conceptual framework that positions public administration as an enabling architecture for the SDGs. It synthesises a body of sixteen recent Nigerian studies on administrative efficiency, accountability, digital governance, social-sector delivery, peace and justice institutions, and infrastructure and urban development, and situates them within wider scholarship on governance capacity and accountability. The paper proposes the Governance-SDG Enabling Architecture (GSEA), in which four enablers (capable administration, accountable institutions, digital and e-governance systems, and inclusive policy) operate through four transmission channels to influence five SDG clusters. Six propositions and a sequenced reform pathway are advanced. The argument is conceptual and does not report new primary data; it is intended to structure future empirical testing and to inform reform sequencing in Nigerian public institutions.

paper_title: Does Turmeric Essential Oil Enhance Curcumin Bioavailability? A Critical Review of the Human Pharmacokinetic Evidence and Its Implications for Curcuma Nutraceuticals
paper_abstract: Reviews of Curcuma essential oils catalogue many biological activities of turmerones, and a recent review states that adding turmeric oil increases curcumin bioavailability 6.93- to 8.2-fold. This review appraises the human evidence behind that claim. Six human pharmacokinetic studies of curcumin formulations containing turmeric oil or turmerones were identiﬁed. Every study favoured the product of its sponsor. The study sponsored by the oil-formulation manufacturer reported a 6.93-fold increase, whereas two randomised, double-blind crossover studies analysed by mass spectrometry found 1.1- to 1.3-fold increases after dose normalisation, and two further studies ranked oil formulations below competing products. The two manufacturer studies reported curcumin peaks of 1.2 to 1.8 µM without separating conjugated from unconjugated curcumin, roughly 600 to 900 times higher than independent measurements of unconjugated curcumin. The 8.2-fold ﬁgure traces to an unpublished document. After a 360 mg dose, plasma ar-turmerone peaked at 3.38 ng/mL, 650 to 1540 times below the concentrations at which it acts in vitro. Current evidence does not support the claim that turmeric oil substantially enhances curcumin bioavailability. Product claims should be withdrawn or tested in independent, factorial trials that measure unconjugated curcumin.

paper_title: Strategies for Early Liberation from Mechanical Ventilation in the Intensive Care Unit After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: Early liberation from mechanical ventilation is an important component of postoperative care after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), but the strategies, extubation-readiness criteria, and reported outcomes remain heterogeneous. This scoping review mapped early ventilator liberation strategies, clinical extubation criteria, and relevant outcomes in adults undergoing CABG. Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR, PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, ScienceDirect, and SciELO were searched from inception to 31 December 2025. Evidence was synthesized descriptively. Of 2374 records identified, 19 studies published between 1977 and 2025 were included. Eleven evaluated automated weaning, five clinical early-extubation protocols, one a non-automated ventilatory strategy, and two observational assessments. Central values for time to extubation ranged from 1.8 to 18.2 h. Eight studies reported a statistically significant reduction in time to extubation, seven found no significant difference, and the comparison was not evaluable in four. Readiness criteria included hemodynamic, gas-exchange, neurological, spontaneous-breathing, and bleeding-control domains, whereas safety outcomes were inconsistently reported. The evidence was heterogeneous and did not establish the superiority of any strategy. Standardized readiness criteria, uniform time definitions, and consistent reporting of clinical and safety outcomes are needed to improve comparability and applicability.

paper_title: Tailoring Lifestyle Medicine in Ethiopia: A Narrative Review on Adapting the Nutritional Pillar to the Ethiopian Context
paper_abstract: Background: Lifestyle medicine (LM) is defined as the discipline of studying how daily habits and practices impact both the prevention and treatment of disease, often in conjunction with pharmaceutical or surgical therapy, to provide an important adjunct to overall health. The pillars of LM comprise nutrition, physical activity, sleep, stress management, avoidance of harmful substances and social connections. Materials and Methods: We conducted a narrative review of the existing literature by searching for literature in PubMed and google scholar. Snowballing of references was also used to identify relevant articles from the articles that came out of the search. We included other studies evaluating Ethiopian dietary habits, staple diets, and EOTC or Islamic (Ramadan) fasting practices. Result: Ethiopian staples like teff injera exhibit low glycemic profiles, aligning with traditional practices that protect against Western-diet-induced metabolic and inflammatory risks. Adherence to Orthodox Christian and Islamic (Ramadan) fasting practices significantly improves mainly cardiometabolic markers, lowering blood pressure, optimizing lipid profiles and injury markers. In addition, these culturally and religious integrated non-pharmacological interventions consistently lower anthropometric measurements, weight, and long-term chronic disease risk profiles. Conclusions: Aligning the nutritional pillar of lifestyle medicine with Ethiopia’s traditional cuisine and religious fasting cycles offers clear health benefits.

paper_title: A Survey of Knowledge Extraction Attacks and Defenses in LLM Agent Ecosystems
paper_abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in handling complex tasks. However, their development and deployment require substantial human and financial resources, making commercial LLM agents valuable intellectual property (IP) assets and raising concerns about their protection. In particular, knowledge extraction (KE) attacks aim to recover protected knowledge or replicate agent components and functionalities without authorization, posing threats to intellectual property and user privacy. Existing surveys primarily focus on model extraction or address information leakage as part of broader security discussions, leaving knowledge extraction across the LLM-based agent ecosystem insufficiently explored. To bridge this gap, we present a systematic survey of knowledge extraction attacks and defenses in LLM-based agents. We propose an asset-oriented taxonomy that categorizes protected knowledge into three groups: agent training assets, deployment-integrated assets, and runtime reusable assets, encompassing training data, LLMs, prompts, RAG systems, agent memory, and skills. For each category, we systematically examine representative attack mechanisms and corresponding defenses, identifying recent advances and outstanding challenges. This survey aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of knowledge extraction threats and inspire future research toward more secure and trustworthy LLM-based agents.

paper_title: From Generative AI Capability to Business Value: A Critical Review of Verification Complements and Value Capture
paper_abstract: Generative artificial intelligence can reduce the cost of producing text, software, and other digital outputs, yet improved task performance does not necessarily produce a viable business model. This review examines the mechanisms connecting generative capabilities to value creation, delivery, and capture. A purposive synthesis brings business-model and digital-transformation theory into dialogue with experimental productivity and creativity studies and recent business-use-case research. The paper distinguishes operating improvements within an existing model from changes to the customer promise, activity system, or revenue logic. It develops a conceptual framework in which useful generation creates potential value, complementary assets enable delivery, verification determines acceptable quality, and bargaining conditions influence who captures the resulting surplus. Four business-model archetypes are examined through their revenue mechanisms, necessary complements, and failure conditions. An explicit cost-per-accepted-outcome model and a hypothetical service example show how inference savings can be offset by review, rework, and provider dependence. Four testable propositions and explicit cost thresholds connect task verifiability, complementary assets, differentiation, and supplier portability to business outcomes. No new field data, causal estimates, or commercial forecasts are reported. The review concludes that research should measure accepted outcomes and distribution of value across stakeholders rather than infer business-model innovation from tool adoption, usage growth, or faster content production alone.

paper_title: Source Address Validation: A Survey of Mechanisms, Measurement, and Deployment
paper_abstract: Source address validation checks whether a packet is entitled to use its claimed Internet Protocol source address at a particular network boundary. Although filtering recommendations have existed since the 1990s, research continues to address incomplete deployment, asymmetric routing, changing address assignments, and limited visibility into enforcement. This survey reviews literature and standards from 1996 through October 2026. We organize mechanisms by the evidence they use: local address bindings, routing information, explicit source announcements, packet authentication, and observed traffic behavior. We distinguish host, prefix, and autonomous system guarantees, and separate packet source validation from route origin validation. We then compare cooperative probing, remote inference, and passive observation, emphasizing the difference between observing successful spoofing and establishing the presence of a filter. An evaluation framework connects false acceptance, false rejection, convergence, implementation cost, and protection under partial deployment. The synthesis identifies three recurring obstacles: the mismatch between forwarding information and source authorization, the mismatch between a measurement sample and a deployment claim, and the mismatch between deployment cost and protection received. We conclude with research directions in authorization semantics, safe rule updates, reproducible evaluation, and verifiable deployment. All reported numerical findings remain attributed to their original studies; this survey contributes no new Internet measurement experiment.

paper_title: Adapting LLM-SC to Living Sacred Heritage: Domain-Specific Extraction, Semantic Networks and Human Evaluation on Pashupatinath Temple Reviews
paper_abstract: Large language model (LLM) pipelines can turn visitor reviews into structured data, but generic schemes may miss rituals, sacred spaces, cultural restrictions and emotionally mixed experiences at living sacred heritage sites. We adapted the LLM-Social Computing (LLM-SC) framework to Pashupatinath Temple, Nepal, by specifying a 12-type entity taxonomy (four original LLM-SC types plus eight sacred-heritage types), four relation types and nine aspect-sentiment dimensions in a GPT-4o extraction prompt, which was applied to a fixed random sample of 2,500 English-language Tripadvisor reviews from a processed corpus of 3,939. The exports contain 11,286 entity, 6,232 aspect-sentiment and 5,590 relation records, covering 2,485, 2,487 and 2,433 reviews, respectively; the eight added sacred-heritage types account for 64.8% of entity records. Against an adjudicated two-annotator reference for 200 reviews, exact normalized surface-and-type matching gave provisional entity scores of 41.0% precision, 21.8% recall and 28.4% micro-F1. Aspect-presence F1 was 53.6% and end-to-end aspect-plus-polarity F1 was 42.6%. Human adjudication supported 153 of 194 first-listed relation candidates (one per review; 78.9%), a candidate-level rate that does not estimate relation recall or whole-graph precision. The contribution is a culturally grounded, domain-specific adaptation with component-wise human evaluation and explicit reproducibility and generalization limitations.

paper_title: Critic's Eye: Review-Grounded Graph Reasoning for Long-Form Motif Discovery
paper_abstract: Deep narrative understanding requires distinguishing what happens from how it is presented, moving beyond the chronological fabula to decode the sjuzet, the discursive organization through which themes are staged. We study this through the recurrence of literary motifs (blood in Macbeth, for instance), where symbolic significance emerges not from local cues, but through repetition-with-variation across the whole work. We operationalize this setting as Computational Motif Discovery, a transductive task that predicts missing line-motif links using the full narrative structure of a play. We propose Critic's Eye, which models the work as a heterogeneous Narrative Topology Graph and performs discriminative inference over global structural evidence. Critic's Eye achieves 84.8% Hit@5 on our benchmark, nearly quadrupling state-of-the-art proprietary foundation models (Gemini-3-pro-preview, ~22.6%). Our analysis reveals that despite massive scaling, sequence-based models hit a "semantic ceiling", struggling to resolve dispersed dependencies. These findings suggest that explicit structural priors are a far more effective inductive bias than parameter scaling for decoding the complex architecture of long-form literature.

paper_title: CIVER: Causal Intervention Verification for Reliable Code Review
paper_abstract: Code review is essential for maintaining software repositories by identifying defects, improving code quality, and supporting reliable software evolution. With the growing adoption of LLM-based coding agents, an increasing number of code contributions and repository changes are generated by these agents. Consequently, LLM-based code review agents are becoming increasingly prevalent to evaluate these contributions and maintain software quality. However, LLM reviewers often generate lengthy reviews containing numerous potential issues, many of which are false positives or lack sufficient evidence. These unreliable reviews can mislead developers and downstream coding agents, motivating the need to distinguish actionable findings from unsupported claims. We propose CIVER, a causal intervention-based framework that identifies the core issues underlying code-review findings and distinguishes genuine defects from false positives. CIVER integrates three modules: a review module assesses findings, an intervention module generates repair-oriented perturbations, and a verifier module scores review reliability. Through joint optimization via expert iteration, the three modules identify genuine defects by responding to targeted repairs while remaining stable under unrelated changes. Extensive experiments on SWE-Review-Bench demonstrate that CIVER correctly identifies 77% of genuine defects through targeted repairs. Cross-project and downstream repair evaluations further demonstrate that CIVER generalizes across repositories and improves coding agents' task success rates, highlighting its effectiveness for reliable automated code review.

paper_title: CyberDual: AI Attackers versus AI Code Reviewers in Real Software Maintenance
paper_abstract: Open-source projects now let AI agents review incoming code, but the code under review may itself come from an AI attacker. We present CyberDual, an arena for this dual role of AI: attacker agents hide an exploitable bug in real maintenance work on widely used open-source projects, and reviewer agents try to find and repair it. Execution decides each match: we rerun the attacker's proof of concept (PoC) on the code that comes out of review. Every attack is new, and the windows can be rebuilt each quarter from the latest upstream history. Three agentic reviewers catch 85-91% of 1,088 valid attacks from six attackers. Yet when the attacker spreads the bug over real upstream commits, about one in six attack slots still ends with a working exploit after review. The strongest attacker has open weights: GLM 5.3 almost never refuses, and its attacks make up 13 of the 28 that get past all three reviewers. When they miss, Claude reviewers mostly approve the attack, while GPT-6-Sol mostly repairs the wrong code; a reviewer from a second vendor catches about two thirds of a Claude reviewer's misses. Beyond a leaderboard, CyberDual has three uses. First, PoC execution gives both sides a reward that agent reports cannot game, so its surviving attacks can train reviewers against stronger attackers. Second, it can gate a release on both scores: Claude Sonnet 5 refuses one in five attack slots, yet attacks about as well as GPT-6-Sol, so refusal alone does not remove attack capability. Third, it can warn the teams behind a deployed reviewer when a new attacker crosses a threshold: GLM 5.3 in Claude Code already gets an exploit past Sonnet 5 in 17% of its attack slots.

paper_title: AlphaIdeaBench: Benchmarking Automated Research Idea Generation under Feasibility Constraints with Peer Review Alignment
paper_abstract: Research ideas are always proposed under resource constraints: a plan must fit the available compute, API credit, and time. Yet evaluations of research-ideation agents mostly score unconstrained novelty or overlap with a published paper, and their LLM judges are rarely checked against peer review. We introduce AlphaIdeaBench, a benchmark of 100 ideation tasks (50 workshop calls for papers and 50 open problems stated in surveys), each paired with an explicit resource budget and a shared proposal schema. An LLM judge scores each proposal on 12 dimensions covering validity, novelty, and feasibility. To validate the judge, we compare its scores on four novelty axes (problem, method, scenario, and insight) with scores derived from reviewer comments on 600 papers from ICLR 2026, NeurIPS 2025, and ICML 2025. For problem and method novelty, Gemini 3.7 Flash is within one point of the reviewer-derived score on 94-97% of papers; agreement on scenario novelty is relatively lower. We evaluate eight published harnesses on a shared backbone and, within one harness, eight backbone LLMs. CoI-Agent obtains the highest overall score, narrowly ahead of SciMON, which leads on method and insight novelty. All harnesses score low on scenario novelty and rarely change the problem setting. The backbone largely determines which open problem a proposal targets, whereas the harness determines whether a proposal addresses one problem or combines several. Weaker backbones such as Llama 4 Scout fail to carry out that harness's strategy and score low on budget feasibility. Finally, when only the budget is varied on three topics, a larger budget changes the experimental setting on compute-intensive topics but only adds tests on an inexpensive one. We release the tasks, rubrics, and scores to foster standardized, reproducible benchmarking of future research-ideation agents under constraints.

paper_title: Can Agentic Code Review Catch Vulnerabilities Before They Are Merged?
paper_abstract: LLM agents have been increasingly adopted for security-focused code review, but existing benchmarks mostly derive the reviewed changes from their later fixes instead of the real-world bug-introducing commits. In this paper, we present SecPRBench, the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating agentic security review on validated real-world code changes. More specifically, we have built an automated agentic pipeline to autonomously harvest, build, and validate massive real-world bug-introducing commits for popular software systems. To ensure precise evaluation, we also adopt LLM-as-a-judge to credit the findings matching ground-truth vulnerabilities. To date, we have collected 265 tasks from nine critical systems, including Firefox, V8, and OpenSSL with millions of lines of code. Across eight frontier models, recall ranges from 32.5% to 78.1%, with Grok 4.6 and GPT-6 sol ranking at the top. Our study also shows that most misses are not simply oversights: in 68% of them, the agent reports on a file that holds the flaw but argues for a different mechanism.
