comments: 29 pages (13 pages main text), 5 figures, 12 tables. Data and code at https://github.com/pth2002/rl-method-tracker and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23495743

paper_title: The More the Better? A Comparison of Single- and Multi-Agent LLM Setups on a Financial Review Task
paper_abstract: Practitioner guidance holds that a large language model reviews a document better when the work is divided among agents. We test a narrow form of it in a controlled comparison of single-agent and multi-agent setups on a financial task, reviewing credit assessment memos against requirements. One agent checks six requirements in one call. A team of three on the same model checks the same memo, two requirements each, in the same words, with no roles or later stage. Labels are known for every requirement on 300 synthetic memos, so misses and false alarms are measured separately. Two primary predictions are tested on four models at a Bonferroni-corrected level. Under an instruction to decide each requirement once, the team catches 0.08 to 0.10 more of the defects that carry an explanation on the three models whose single agent misses some, at the corrected level on two. It raises more false alarms on all four, at the corrected level on three. Balanced accuracy, an exploratory measure, changes by 0.02 or less, and the team uses 2.2 to 2.4 times the tokens. Showing each agent the requirements it was not given reduces the added false alarms on the two Claude models, at the corrected level on one. In exploratory comparisons, sampling the single agent three times and flagging on any draw gives higher balanced accuracy than the team on those models, and the team's results depend on the instruction.

paper_title: Reinforcement learning for hardware acceleration and system-level optimization on FPGA and integrated-circuit platforms: A survey
paper_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables adaptive and autonomous decision-making in embedded, edge, and heterogeneous computing systems. Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) and integrated circuits (ICs) offer low latency, energy efficiency, and architectural flexibility for RL deployment, while introducing challenges in resource constraints, implementation complexity, and hardware-algorithm co-design. This review surveys more than 100 studies on RL implementations across FPGA and IC platforms, emphasizing architectures, implementation strategies, performance evaluation, and applications. The literature is organized by RL family, including model-based Markov decision processes, classical value-based methods, deep RL, actor-critic, policy-gradient, and multi-agent approaches. We further classify studies by abstraction level, hardware realization strategy, and application domain, examining how RL algorithms map onto reconfigurable and fixed hardware. Unlike surveys restricted to particular algorithms or platforms, this work provides a unified analysis of FPGA and IC implementations, covering acceleration, reconfigurable architectures, energy-aware control, and system-level optimization. Comparative assessments consider resource utilization, latency, throughput, power consumption, and reported performance gains. Finally, we identify recurring architectural patterns, practical limitations, open challenges, and research directions for efficient RL-driven hardware systems. The survey offers a consolidated reference for researchers developing and evaluating RL solutions on specialized hardware.

paper_title: BCI & AI for Cognitively-Aware Learning: A Review of Technologies, Tools, and Applications
paper_abstract: This article presents a comprehensive review of technologies, tools, and applications in the field of brain-computer interfaces (BCI) and artificial intelligence (AI) for developing cognitively adaptive learning environments. Unlike prior reviews that treat BCI hardware, AI decoding models, and pedagogical deployment as separate topics, this review develops an integrated cross-layer taxonomy linking hardware constraints, AI architecture requirements, and classroom deployment conditions. Emphasis is placed on the transition from cumbersome laboratory systems to wearable hybrid solutions combining electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), as well as textile sensors that offer a favorable trade-off between neurophysiological signal quality and mobility in real-world classroom settings. The review includes a detailed analysis of modern AI architectures, transformer-based models for processing non-stationary neural signals, and Siamese neural networks implementing a few-shot learning paradigm to address the calibration problem associated with new users. It further proposes a unified state-estimation framework integrating cognitive load, attention, and affect into a single formalization for closed-loop adaptive learning systems. The review concludes with a critical analysis of fundamental barriers to scalability, signal instability, mental state privacy issues, and the risk of a neurocognitive divide arising from unequal access to technology. The authors argue that the future of neuroeducation lies in the symbiotic interaction of humans and AI, supported by unified international standards and the convergence of BCI with large language models (LLM) for predictive communication.

paper_title: Aquagenic Syringeal Acrokeratoderma Successfully Managed with Topical Glycopyrronium: A Case and Review of the Literature
paper_abstract: Acquired aquagenic syringeal acrokeratoderma (ASA) is a rare dermatological disorder characterised by transient oedematous papules and palmar wrinkling following water exposure. Multiple treatment modalities have been described, however evidence supporting effective therapies is limited. We report a case of a 21-year-old Indian male with a 2-year history of painful palmar wrinkling, tingling, and stinging occurring approximately 15 minutes after water exposure, with associated pruritus and peeling following prolonged immersion. Clinical findings were consistent with acquired ASA, and investigations excluded systemic disease. Initial treatment with topical 20% aluminium chloride was discontinued because of excessive dryness. Subsequent treatment with topical glycopyrronium bromide 2% spray produced a 50% reduction in symptom severity without adverse effects, with sustained improvement over 1.5 years. This favourable response supports current evidence for a pathogenic role for eccrine gland dysfunction and sweating in ASA and suggests that epithelial transmembrane channelopathy with sweat leakage may contribute to disease development. Treatments targeting these pathways may therefore be effective strategies and topical glycopyrronium bromide can be a therapeutic consideration in ASA. Further studies are needed to validate these mechanisms and establish optimal management strategies.

paper_title: Residual Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk After Bariatric Surgery: Fibrosis Regression, Metabolic Improvement, and Implications for Surveillance—A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Background and Objectives: Metabolic and bariatric surgery improves obesity and metabolic dys-function-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), but its effect on the residual risk of hepatocellu- lar carcinoma (HCC) is less clearly defined. This narrative review examines the relationship between postoperative metabolic improvement, fibrosis regression, and HCC risk, with particular attention to surveillance. Materials and Methods: A targeted literature search identified clinical studies, mechanistic investigations, and professional guidance relevant to bariatric surgery, MASLD, and HCC. Results: Randomized and paired-biopsy studies support improvement in steatohepatitis, whereas observational cohorts associate surgery with lower HCC occurrence and fewer major adverse liver outcomes. These findings address different endpoints and should not be treated as interchangeable evidence of cancer prevention. Advanced fibrosis can persist despite substantial weight loss and resolution of steatohepatitis. Conversely, the absolute postoperative HCC risk among patients with documented fibrosis regression remains insufficiently characterized. The available evidence does not establish a postoperative biochemical, elastographic, or histological threshold at which surveillance can safely be stopped in patients with established cirrhosis. Conclusion: Surveillance decisions should therefore remain anchored to the underlying liver disease, treatment eligibility, and applicable guidance rather than weight loss alone. Noncirrhotic advanced fibrosis requires individualized assessment because professional recommendations differ and evidence is limited. Future studies should report HCC separately from composite liver outcomes and evaluate risk according to baseline and postoperative fibrosis, metabolic trajectories, and surveillance exposure. Bariatric surgery may modify the course of liver disease, but metabolic improvement should not be equated with elimination of carcinogenic risk.

paper_title: Extension Services and the Social Sustainability Mission of Higher Education Institutions (HEIs): A Critical Integrative Review
paper_abstract: Higher education institutions (HEIs) are increasingly expected to contribute to sustainable development through research, instruction, and community engagement. However, contemporary higher education systems have become progressively research-oriented, prioritizing publication productivity, citation metrics, and institutional rankings. While these developments have expanded academic knowledge production, they have also contributed to a growing disconnect between knowledge generation and societal utilization. Within this context, extension services remain comparatively underprioritized despite their potential role in translating academic knowledge into meaningful community impact. This paper presents a critical integrative review of extension services in higher education, focusing on their conceptual evolution, institutional positioning, and contribution to the social sustainability mission of universities. The review examines how extension services have evolved from traditional technology-transfer and outreach models toward broader paradigms of community engagement, knowledge democratization, and sustainability-oriented development. It further analyzes the institutional marginalization of extension services within increasingly research-driven academic systems. Findings suggest that extension services remain insufficiently theorized and institutionally undervalued despite their critical role in promoting equitable knowledge access and community-centered development. The paper argues that extension services should be repositioned as central mechanisms through which HEIs translate academic knowledge into sustainable societal impact.

paper_title: When Coding Agents Outpace Review: Evaluating PRD-Driven Development in Mature Enterprise Repositories
paper_abstract: Coding agents increasingly undertake development tasks in mature enterprise repositories, yet existing benchmarks offer limited insight into whether they fulfill complete Product Requirement Documents (PRDs) and where delivery breaks down. Issue resolution and development from scratch leave incremental PRD fulfillment underexplored, while isolated tests provide incomplete evidence of business and integration requirements. We introduce PACE, a benchmark of 43 enterprise tasks with 750 expert-audited Code Points. It combines requirement reconstruction, criterion construction, and evidence-based evaluation to measure PRD fulfillment and connect delivery gaps to agent behavior. Across 11 model--scaffold configurations, most scores fall between 52.1 and 78.1; GPT-5.6-Sol achieves the highest complete-delivery rate of 14.0\%. Incomplete implementation and missing integration are the principal bottlenecks: producing individual components does not ensure a complete delivery. Evaluation achieves 95.2\% agreement with expert consensus, with lower case-level variation across judging records than repeated executions. Beyond model comparison, the benchmark provides actionable feedback for harness refinement: diagnosis guides targeted improvements, and successive harness releases raise mean performance from 59.4 to 63.0 using the same model and task suite. Code is available at https://github.com/TianqiLiu1/PACE-Bench.

paper_title: Leveraging Mental Models for Human-Centered Explanations: A Systematic Design Approach Illustrated by Explainable Fake Review Identification
paper_abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) often prioritizes model fidelity over user intelligibility, yielding explanations that satisfy technical transparency yet fail to support human sense-making. We propose a human-centered approach, MIND-X (Mental-model INtegrated Design for eXplainability), which aligns explanations with users' mental models, commonsense concepts, and judgment heuristics. Using fake review detection as a case study, we contribute: (1) a qualitative study (n=10) that elicits how people assess review credibility and produces an actionable, design-guiding taxonomy of perceptual cues; (2) a set of design principles that link those cues to explanation strategies and prompt LLMs to generate adaptive, language-based explanations; and (3) a quantitative evaluation (n=166) showing that these explanations offer distinct advantages over token-level transparency methods widely used in explainable text classification in terms of understandability, satisfaction, perceived trust, persuasiveness, and decision-making support. Rather than claiming general superiority, our evaluation illustrates how grounding explanations in users' everyday reasoning practices can produce more intelligible and context-sensitive accounts. Our findings advance human-centered explanation design beyond a mere "gloss of transparency," demonstrating that a mental-model-aligned design process can improve intelligibility and support accountability across user-centered explanation tasks.
comments: 38 pages, 10 figures, 8 tables. Keywords: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI); Human-centered AI; Mental models; Fake review detection; User-centered explanation design; Natural language explanations; Cognitive heuristics

paper_title: Towards Next-Generation Architectures of Large Language Models: A Survey
paper_abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have advanced rapidly through increases in model scale, data, and computation, while their underlying architectures have also undergone substantial evolution. Beyond the canonical Transformer architecture, recent designs seek greater efficiency, scalability, and flexibility by rethinking how sequence information is processed, represented, and transformed. We survey efficient attention and state management, modern recurrent and other linear-complexity sequence models, Mixture-of-Experts architectures, and advances in activation functions, normalization, residual connections, positional encoding, and tokenization. We also cover multi-token prediction and adaptive and recurrent depth. Across these areas, we highlight key design principles and trade-offs among representational power, optimization stability, and computational cost. Complementing this component-wise treatment, we take a system-level perspective. We trace representative open-weight LLM families to identify recurring patterns in how architectural choices are combined, and synthesize these developments along four dimensions—processing structure, transformation dynamics, state management, and output commitment—characterizing how recent designs preserve, refine, or relax the assumptions of the canonical decoder. Together, this survey aims to provide a systematic overview of LLM architectural evolution and to chart pathways toward next-generation designs.

paper_title: Review of Health Knowledge Graphs for Clinical Decision Support: Construction, LLM-Grounded Reasoning, and Applications
paper_abstract: Health Knowledge Graphs (Health-KGs) structure heterogeneous medical information from Electronic Health Records (EHRs), the biomedical literature, and clinical guidelines into machine-reasonable form, and have become a foundation for clinical decision support. This work reviews the construction and application of Health-KGs following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, organizing the literature along three axes representation, extraction, and integration and situating it against prior biomedical-KG reviews. We examine knowledge-representation learning and graph-embedding models, named-entity recognition, disambiguation, and linking, and cross-source integration, together with the principal EHR datasets and clinical language models that underpin them. A distinguishing focus is the shift toward large language models (LLMs): we synthesize LLM-driven entity and relation extraction, retrieval and graph-augmented clinical reasoning, and the factuality and hallucination constraints that govern their safe use an axis not addressed by prior EHR-focused reviews. We further reviewed applications spanning drug development and clinical trials, diagnosis and prediction, treatment recommendation, question answering, and health-policy compliance. Finally, we identify the central open challenges: the absence of a standardized, openly governed Health-KG benchmark; heterogeneous and temporally evolving clinical data; multimodal fusion; and privacy-preserving, reproducible construction. This review is intended as a roadmap for data scientists, medical-informatics and AI researchers, and healthcare practitioners.

paper_title: Technology Assessment, Techno-Economic Evaluation and Risk Analysis of Dynamic Line Rating for Overhead Transmission Lines: A PRISMA-Based Systematic Literature Review
paper_abstract: Dynamic line rating (DLR) adapts the ratings of overhead lines to actual or forecast weather and conductor conditions, supplementing or replacing conservative static line ratings (SLRs) when conditions allow. Utilities must judge their maturity, economics and risks together. This systematic review, reported following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020, retrieved 1234 records from IEEE Xplore, Scopus, SpringerLink and supplementary searches with the AI-assisted tool Consensus; 363 studies published in 2010–2026 were included and coded into technology assessment (n = 142), techno-economic evaluation (n = 156) and risk/reliability assessment (n = 145). Field studies in temperate, wind-exposed systems report gains commonly cited at 20–40% (5–10% for ambient-adjusted ratings), whereas tropical studies report smaller margins and ratings below the SLR during heat waves. System-level simulations report operating-cost reductions of about 3–16%, but DLR-specific costs are rarely itemised. Only 3 studies were coded as addressing all three dimensions, and cost–benefit analyses with explicit risk quantification are rare. Twelve deployment and operational risks were consolidated into a literature-informed likelihood–consequence matrix, in which rating overestimation and unaccounted low-wind/heat-wave conditions ranked highest. A conceptual five-stage framework is proposed to help utilities, particularly in tropical power systems, move from line screening to risk-informed deployment decisions.

paper_title: Wood Ash Fertilisation and Heavy Metal Dynamics in Boreal and Temperate Forest Soils: A Systematic Review of Short- and Long-Term Evidence
paper_abstract: Wood ash returns base cations to forest soil, but also brings heavy metals. This systematic review assessed the impact of applying ash at operational rates on the content, mobility and leaching of heavy metals in soil in temperate and boreal forest soils in Europe and North America. Of 99 studies selected, 15 included both an ash treatment and measurements of metals. Ash application has been shown to raise pH in the organic horizon by 0.5 to 1.6 units and to increase base saturation. Cadmium, zinc, copper, nickel and chromium were shown to accumulate in the forest floor. However, no studies reported metal accumulation in soil solution at a depth of 50 cm after intervals of up to seventeen years, and no studies reported on groundwater. Above approximately 9 t ha-1, soil solution cadmium, aluminium mobilisation and soil pH dropping below that of the control occurred concurrently after the fourth year, indicating a threshold and the depletion of ash alkalinity through nitrification. Using ash to retain rather than remove heavy metals such as cadmium is problematic, as ash applications can represent several years of atmospheric deposition. Moreover, cadmium remains in a pool highly dependent on pH, C/N balance and an unregulated retention period.

paper_title: Health Effects of Nature-Based Mindfulness Interventions in Schools: A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: Schools are an integral setting for early prevention and promotion of mental health and well-being among children and adolescents. Nature-based mindfulness (NBM) interventions combine mindfulness practices with exposure to nature and may be a promising approach to supporting children and adolescent health and well-being. However, no review studies have comprehensively examined the evidence on NBM interventions in schools among children and adolescents. This scoping review summarizes the current evidence on school-based NBM interventions that assess child and adolescent health outcomes and discusses their potential to impact health and well-being. The ten studies included in the scoping review reported associations between NBM interventions and improvements in mental well-being, social-emotional functioning, educational outcomes, and connection to nature. Physical health outcomes were examined in only one study and were not statistically significant. Findings from this review highlight the potential of NBM interventions to support health and well-being among children and adolescents in school settings, while also emphasizing the need for more rigorous methodologies and study designs to strengthen the evidence base to guide equitable and effective implementation.

paper_title: TRPS1 in Breast Carcinoma: A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Determining the mammary origin of a metastatic or poorly differentiated carcinoma is a frequent challenge in surgical pathology. Conventional breast markers (GATA3, GCDFP-15 and mammaglobin) lose sensitivity in triple-negative and metaplastic breast carcinoma. TRPS1 (trichorhinophalangeal syndrome type 1), an atypical GATA-family transcription factor, was proposed in 2020–2021 as an immunohistochemical marker of breast lineage. This narrative review summarizes the literature up to October 2026 on TRPS1 biology, its diagnostic performance across breast carcinoma subtypes, its expression in non-mammary neoplasms and its place in current diagnostic panels. TRPS1 shows nuclear positivity in 86–99% of breast carcinomas, including triple-negative and metaplastic tumors, in which it outperforms GATA3. It is almost always negative in urothelial carcinoma, a GATA3-positive mimic of breast carcinoma. However, large studies have demonstrated expression in squamous cell carcinomas, salivary gland tumors, gynecologic carcinomas, cutaneous adnexal neoplasms and sarcomas, with overall specificities of 58–74% in recent series. Apocrine, triple-negative neuroendocrine and acinic cell carcinomas are usually negative. TRPS1 is the most sensitive breast-lineage marker currently available, particularly in triple-negative breast cancer, but it is not specific. It should be interpreted together with morphology, clinical history and a panel that includes GATA3 and markers relevant to the differential diagnosis.

paper_title: Polygenic Risk Scores for Pancreatic Cancer Risk Prediction and Early Detection: A Systematic Evidence Review of Clinical Utility
paper_abstract: Background/Objectives: Pancreatic cancer carries a five-year relative survival of 13%. Polygenic risk scores (PRS) rank inherited susceptibility across common variants. Prior syntheses pooled PRS association and discrimination, but none asked whether a PRS changes a clinical decision. We synthesized evidence on the clinical utility of PRS for pancreatic cancer risk assessment. Methods: In this PROSPERO-registered review (CRD42024511326), we searched four databases through May 11, 2026, for studies evaluating a PRS for primary pancreatic cancer risk in adults, alone or with clinical predictors. We recorded discrimination as the prerequisite for utility and organized utility across five prespecified domains: threshold-based accuracy, incremental value, calibrated absolute risk, decision-analytic output, and economic impact. We synthesized narratively and appraised risk of bias with PROBAST. Results: Forty-three studies met the inclusion and exclusion criteria, including 25 from the UK Biobank. Ten of 16 standalone discrimination estimates fell between 0.56 and 0.64. Adding PRS to a clinical model increased discrimination by at most 0.05 in general populations. Combined PRS and clinical models exceeded 0.80 only in three diabetes-focused studies. Six studies reported calibration, four reclassification, two decision-curve net benefit, none cost-effectiveness, and 20 had no translational milestone. Thirteen studies were at high risk of bias, with 11 in the analysis domain. Conclusions: Pancreatic cancer PRS discriminates modestly alone and adds most where prior risk is highest. Actionable use awaits an externally validated absolute-risk model with a prespecified threshold and a decision analysis.

paper_title: Virtual Reality (VR)-Based Safety Training for Post-Disaster Responders and Workers: A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: Post-disaster responders and workers operate in hazardous environments that require rapid decision-making, hazard recognition, and effective safety training. Virtual reality (VR) has emerged in recent years as an innovative tool for immersive occupational safety and health education. This scoping review systematically examines peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025 on the use of VR for safety training among personnels across a broad range of fields who perform or are trained to perform disaster and emergency response functions. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, five electronic databases (PubMed, ProQuest Central, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and ERIC) were searched, resulting in 2,202 identified articles; 19 of which met the inclusion criteria after screening and eligibility assessments. The reviewed studies suggest that VR-based safety training, which uses fully immersive simulated environments, can improve learner engagement, situational awareness, hazard recognition, decision-making, and confidence in disaster response scenarios. Several studies have reported higher user satisfaction and increased realism compared with traditional instructional methods such as classroom-based instruction or mock drills. However, the evidence remains heterogeneous, with limitations including small sample sizes, technical challenges, limited scenario diversity, and insufficient long-term evaluation of training outcomes. Overall, VR is a promising supplement to traditional safety and health training for post-disaster responders and workers; however, additional longitudinal research and large-scale studies are needed to further evaluate its effectiveness and long-term applicability in various disaster-response settings.

paper_title: C-MOP: A Narrative Review and Clinical Framework for Adjunctive Repurposed-Drug Therapy in Active Cancer
paper_abstract: Cancer metabolic adaptability and treatment resistance provide a rationale for evaluating coordinated interventions across complementary tumor and host processes. This narrative review examines five medications used within the Cancer Metabolic Optimization Protocol (C-MOP) - metformin, atorvastatin, doxycycline, mebendazole, and ivermectin - and describes a physician-directed framework for adjunctive use in adults with active cancer. The central hypothesis is that complementary effects on energy regulation, mevalonate signaling, mitochondrial function, microtubule dynamics, and adaptive stress responses may constrain compensatory pathways and enhance sensitivity to conventional treatment. Selected experimental combinations and early clinical experience with other multi-agent repurposing regimens support investigation of this strategy. Evidence for the individual agents is heterogeneous: metformin and statins have the largest human evidence base, with mixed or negative randomized findings in several settings; doxycycline and mebendazole have predominantly preclinical, translational, and early-phase support. Ivermectin remains the most experimental component, with predominantly preclinical evidence and evolving dosing and long-term safety questions in oncology. The framework links agent selection to patient-specific goals, conventional oncology treatment, organ function, interactions, sequential initiation, monitoring, and reassessment of treatment burden. The clinical benefit of the complete five-agent regimen remains to be established. By defining the combination rationale, patient selection, individualized implementation, and safety procedures, C-MOP provides a foundation for consistent clinical reporting and prospective evaluation.

paper_title: A Review of Virtual Power Plant Technology and Practice Development in China: Progress, Challenges, and Outlook
paper_abstract: As an important vehicle for resource integration in the construction of new power systems, the virtual power plant (VPP) has moved from the demonstration and pilot stage into a critical transition period of standardized construction and market-oriented operation. This paper systematically reviews the technological development trajectory and the practical progress of VPPs in China. At the technical level, key advances are reviewed across three core domains: resource perception and adjustable potential assessment; optimal dispatch and control strategies (covering centralized, distributed, and reinforcement learning-based methods); and cloud–edge–terminal platform architecture and information security. At the practical level, the paper traces the policy evolution from the early demand response pilots to the 2025 Guiding Opinions on Accelerating the Development of Virtual Power Plants, surveys grid-led and third-party-aggregator demonstration projects, and analyzes business models and pathways for participation in electricity markets. On this basis, the key challenges facing Chinese VPPs in technical standardization, market access, regulatory frameworks, and data security are analyzed, and international experience from Europe (Next Kraftwerke, Flexitricity), North America (FERC Order 2222), and Australia (Tesla VPP) is summarized. Finally, future development pathways are discussed from four directions: technological trends (digital twins and the integration of large language models), the improvement of market mechanisms, the construction of the policy and standards system, and the cultivation of a multi-stakeholder industrial ecosystem.

paper_title: TrustChain-Review: A Risk-Adaptive Blockchain and Game-Theoretic Framework for Trustworthy AI-Assisted Code Review
paper_abstract: AI-assisted software development is reshaping how code is generated, reviewed, tested, and maintained. However, the increasing use of AI coding assistants introduces new trust and quality-assurance challenges. Developers may submit AI-generated code without sufficient verification, reviewers may approve changes superficially, and platform-level reputation scores may be affected by biased, incomplete, or malicious feedback. Many existing code-review and reputation mechanisms remain centralized, weakly auditable, or insufficiently adaptive to strategic behaviour among developers, reviewers, and platform operators. To address these limitations, this paper proposes TrustChain-Review, a blockchain-enabled game-theoretic incentive framework for trustworthy AI-assisted code review. The framework integrates three complementary layers. First, a blockchain-based evidence layer is proposed to record or reference review activities, code-change metadata, review comments, dataset-observed quality-related evidence, and reputation updates in a tamper-resistant manner. The empirical part of this study uses dataset-observed fields from the Diff Quality Estimation dataset, while test outcomes, vulnerability reports, and post-merge defect signals are considered future deployment-level evidence. Second, a game-theoretic incentive layer models the strategic interactions among developers, reviewers, and the platform, capturing trade-offs between effort, reward, penalty, transparency cost, and reputation gain. Third, a risk-adaptive governance mechanism determines when the expected trust, auditability, and risk-reduction benefits of evidence-based review justify its additional operational cost. This decision rule connects contribution risk, developer effort, reviewer reliability, reputation effects, and platform governance cost within a unified game-theoretic framework. The proposed framework aims to improve the reliability of reputation scores, reduce the impact of low-quality or dishonest feedback, and encourage cooperative behaviour in AI-assisted software ecosystems. The framework is evaluated through a controlled simulation calibrated with empirical characteristics extracted from the Diff Quality Estimation dataset, including balanced review-need labels, patch-length statistics, review-comment availability, and language-metadata coverage. The results show that TrustChain-Review improves reputation accuracy, trust convergence, malicious review detection, and superficial review detection compared with simple reputation, centralized reputation, blockchain-only, and static-incentive baselines, while introducing a higher governance-cost trade-off. These findings suggest that evidence-based governance is most valuable when contribution risk and trust requirements are sufficiently high to justify its additional cost, while simpler governance may remain more appropriate for low-risk review settings.

paper_title: Validating LLM-generated political networks with survey-reported partisan exposure
paper_abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate human behavior in social science research, including decisions, interactions, and social relationships. However, in network formation tasks, existing evaluations often focus on aggregate network properties, while networks with plausible structural properties may still fail to reproduce individuals' social and political environments. Here, we generate LLM-based political networks using personas sampled from the nationally representative ANES 2020--2022 Social Media Study and use respondents' survey-reported partisan exposure as an empirical benchmark for the political environments generated for the corresponding personas. We first characterize the structural properties and political assortativity of the generated networks, and then compare ego-level partisan exposure with the survey. We find that the structure and political assortativity of the generated networks vary across experimental configurations. More importantly, when comparing generated partisan exposure with the survey, some models generate stronger separation between Democratic and Republican egos than reported in the survey, with higher same-party and lower cross-party exposure, while others mainly underestimate Republican exposure across ego groups. Moreover, networks with similar political assortativity can still generate different partisan environments around the same personas, including among networks with plausible structural properties. Finally, generated networks show group-specific errors, under- or overestimating exposure to either Democrats or Republicans for specific social groups. These findings show that evaluating LLM-based social simulations only through aggregate outcomes can hide errors in the local environments through which those outcomes emerge, highlighting the importance of validation at both aggregate and individual levels.

paper_title: Detection of false positives by human reviewers depends on the face recognition algorithm and its security configuration
paper_abstract: Integration of artificial intelligence (AI) technology into identity workflows, such as automated face recognition (FR), has enhanced operational capabilities, with FR algorithms achieving super-human scale and accuracy. However, these gains can make human oversight of FR more difficult, raising questions about the effectiveness of these human-AI teams. We measured human reviewers' ability to detect false positive errors made by commercial FR algorithms across varying security configurations. Using a novel dataset, the Difficult Facial Image Comparison Test (DFICT), derived from false positives made by four comparable commercial face recognition algorithms, we measured the ability of 801human reviewers to detect algorithmic false positives across three security configurations, representing operationally relevant biometric thresholds. Our findings show that human reviewers can reduce algorithmic false positives, but performance declines at stricter security thresholds. Further, reviewer performance varied by algorithm indicating that some algorithms are more compatible with human oversight. We suggest that biometric systems should be designed to account for human reviewers' variable effectiveness, particularly in high-security applications. Our findings should be considered during algorithm selection and inform human oversight strategies to minimize AI-related risks in operational FR deployments.

paper_title: Wearable and Marker-Less Sensing for Load and Technique Quantification in Combat Sports: A Scoping Review, with Fencing as an Illustrative Case
paper_abstract: Combat sports require measurement systems that tolerate contact and protective equipment. Following JBI and PRISMA-ScR guidance, this scoping review mapped how wearable, marker-less, and equipment-embedded sensors have been used to quantify load, physiological response, and technique in boxing, judo, wrestling, taekwondo, and fencing, and what measurement-property evidence accompanies their outputs. PubMed and IEEE Xplore (2015–2026) were searched and supplemented by citation searching; a second reviewer screened a random 20% sample (κ = 0.75). We included 222 reports, 39 of them charted from abstracts, which most often used physiological wearables, followed by inertial and equipment-embedded sensors. Only 44 reports (20%) presented strong evidence for the analysed output (criterion agreement, between-day reliability, verified event detection or testing on unseen athletes), and 28 (13%) weak evidence only. Of 38 machine-learning evaluations, 12 tested athletes not used for training. Four reports (three in boxing) paired head-impact exposure with an acute health endpoint and 11 recorded mechanical surrogates only; none linked sensor exposure to subsequent injury. We propose a 14-item reporting checklist adapted from existing guidance.

paper_title: Looped Language Models: A Survey and Meta-Analysis of Recurrent-Depth Transformers
paper_abstract: Looped language models apply one shared block of Transformer layers repeatedly to the same tokens. Their effective depth, the number of layer applications per token, can grow without adding parameters and can be chosen at inference time. Recurrent depth is thus a way to scale test-time compute in latent space instead of in generated tokens. The idea appears under many names, including looped Transformers, LoopLMs, recurrent-depth models, Universal Transformers, Mixture-of-Recursions, and recursive reasoning models such as HRM and TRM. In two years it has moved from synthetic tasks to open models such as Huginn and Ouro and to pretraining on up to 28 trillion tokens. According to press reports, it is also used in a frontier-lab model. Its literature has split across architecture, training, systems, theory and safety. We present the first survey dedicated to looped language models, built on a systematic corpus of 557 core papers screened from 7,323 candidates. We introduce a unified prelude–core–coda formalism that makes explicit how parameters, compute, memory and depth are counted. We organize the field from design, training and scaling to inference systems, theory, mechanisms, capabilities, other modalities and safety. A meta-analysis classifies 822 verified empirical claims by comparison regime. It shows that most apparent contradictions about whether “a recurrence is worth a layer” come from comparing parameter-matched with compute-matched results. The evidence fits one reading, in which a recurrence is worth less than a fresh block of parameters. Looping therefore helps when parameters are the limiting resource and hurts when it replaces them at fixed compute. We derive a research agenda from measured gaps, including the absence of work on robustness, alignment and privacy. We release the corpus, the extraction records with verbatim evidence for every number, and the claims ledger.

paper_title: Application of the Portable Electromagnetic Impact Seismic Source in Seismic Engineering Survey
paper_abstract: Traditional seismic excitation sources often perform poorly in complex urban settings. In this study, an innovative portable electromagnetic impact source is introduced. The design and manufacturing principles are detailed, and the performance is verified through comprehensive simulations. Furthermore, field experiments are conducted to assess the device's energy output, frequency range, and imaging accuracy in real-world engineering surveys. Experimental results show that compared with the traditional sledgehammer source, the electromagnetic impact seismic source has stronger excitation energy (the impact kinetic energy is about 1218 J, which is about 5 times that of the 24-pound sledgehammer source), and a wider frequency band (the widest range is 0.1–1200 Hz), which is critical for detection depth and accuracy. The obtained seismic data have a wider frequency band and a higher reflected wave signal-to-noise ratio, which effectively improves the resolution and detection depth of underground anomalies. The spatial distribution of air-raid shelters can be clearly identified based on the transient amplitude profile, which verifies the applicability and reliability of the electromagnetic impact source in seismic engineering surveys and demonstrates its good application prospects in the field of underground space detection. It is especially suitable for accurately detecting caves and air-raid shelters that are prone to collapse in urban road environments.

paper_title: Evolutionary Status of Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome Virus (PRRSV) Variants in Swine Farms in Lima, Peru: A Review of Molecular and Epidemiological Evidence through 2026
paper_abstract: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome (PRRS) is a major economically important disease affecting the global swine industry. Its etiological agent, porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV), exhibits substantial genetic diversity driven by mutation, recombination, and selective pressures. Following taxonomic revisions by the International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses, PRRSV isolates are classified into Betaarterivirus europensis and Betaarterivirus americense. In Peru, the molecular and epidemiological evolution of PRRSV in Lima’s swine farms remains insufficiently characterized. This review aimed to characterize the evolutionary dynamics of PRRSV variants circulating in Lima through 2026. A narrative review with a systematic search strategy was conducted following PRISMA 2020 principles. Searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, SciELO, Redalyc, LILACS, and GenBank identified 200 records, of which 60 met the eligibility criteria. Studies addressed global taxonomy and molecular biology (50.0%), international evolutionary dynamics (25.0%), South American epidemiology (8.3%), and PRRSV evolution in Lima (16.7%). Evidence suggests three periods: European-genotype detection (1998-2012); increased epidemiological characterization and reports of genetically distinct or highly virulent lineages (2013-2022); and diversification of B. americense, including NADC34-like sublineages and field-strain recombination evidence (2022-2026). These findings support sustained genomic surveillance, whole-genome sequencing, and coordinated molecular monitoring across South America.

paper_title: Oxygen Delivery, Tissue Function, and Veterinary Oxygen Therapeutics: A Narrative Review of William W. Muirʹs Scientiﬁc Contributions
paper_abstract: The scientific work of Professor William W. Muir addresses a fundamental problem in oxygen therapeutics: increasing oxygen transport capacity does not necessarily mean that oxygen reaches the tissues where it is needed. Over several decades, Muir investigated cardiovascular physiology, respiratory gas exchange, hemorrhagic shock, microvascular perfusion, hemoglobin-based oxygen carriers (HBOCs), and tissue oxygenation. His scientific involvement with Biopure, collaboration with Carl W. Rausch, and subsequent reported advisory activities in veterinary product development form an important part of this history. This article traces the development of these ideas and their experimental evaluation, leading to a proposed next step: Precision Oxygen Therapeutics based on Biological Hemoglobin Oxygen Carrier (BHOC), with oxygen delivery treated as a distinct therapeutic function rather than an attempt to replace blood.

paper_title: Dynamic Mosaicism Involving a Ring Chromosome 2 in a 4-Year-Old Male: Case Report and Literature Review
paper_abstract: Ring chromosomes (RCs) are rare structural chromosomal abnormalities caused by terminal breaks and fusion of chromosome ends, occurring in approximately 1 in 50,000 live births. They are often associated with “ring chromosome syndrome,” characterized by growth restriction, mild dysmorphism, and variable intellectual disability, even without large deletions. Ring chromosome 2 is exceptionally rare, with fewer than 20 reported cases and limited molecular characterization. We report a 4-year-old male with proportional growth restriction, mild facial dysmorphism, and delayed expressive speech. Cytogenetic analysis identified a mosaic ring chromosome 2, and fluorescence in situ hybridization demonstrated preserved subtelomeric regions. However, array comparative genomic hybridization revealed a 46 kb deletion at 2p25.3 involving the protein-coding gene FAM110C. This case broadens the phenotypic and molecular spectrum of ring chromosome 2 and underscores the value of combining cytogenetic and high-resolution genomic techniques to detect cryptic imbalances contributing to clinical presentation.

paper_title: Clogging-Induced Hydro-Mechanical Deterioration of Stone Columns in Liquefiable Soils Under Seismic Loading: A Critical Review, Quantitative Synthesis and Coupled-Modeling Agenda
paper_abstract: Stone columns mitigate earthquake-induced liquefaction through three mechanisms: densification, shear-stress redistribution, and radial drainage. The first two are established at installation and are permanent; the third is not. Fines migrate into the column under cyclic hydraulic gradients, permeability falls, drainage resistance rises, and the pore pressure the design was intended to suppress re-accumulates. An improved site therefore migrates from a three-mechanism to a two-mechanism system during its service life, a transition current design practice does not recognize. This paper synthesizes that degradation quantitatively: a structured database of test configurations was extracted from a corpus of 188 records and pooled using a study-clustered random-effects procedure. The pooled bearing capacity ratio is 1.52 and the pooled settlement ratio 0.75, but every contributing configuration was tested statically, so the quantities the literature reports densely are not the quantities seismic design depends upon. That mismatch between what the literature measures densely and what seismic design actually requires is the principal empirical finding of this synthesis. Shaking table evidence shows ordinary columns clogging so rapidly that liquefaction onset is delayed by about one second relative to untreated ground at low base acceleration, after which the columns punch 26 to 43 percent of their length into the deposit; encased and sand-filtered columns settle with the ground by 9 percent and prevent liquefaction at four times that acceleration. Analytical models admitting clogging report post-earthquake settlement increases up to 229 percent and second-event pore-pressure ratios more than 36 percent higher. Against this, every fully coupled numerical framework in current use holds column permeability constant by assumption. The paper formalizes a clogging-induced hydro-mechanical deterioration framework with governing equations, shows the classical filter rule and the seismic drainage requirement to be mutually incompatible, and specifies the falsifiable experiment that would close the gap. Two limitations bound these pooled values and are stated here rather than buried: the bearing capacity ratio rests on three independent studies and the settlement ratio on one, so neither should be read as a stable population estimate, and both derive from static tests and therefore cannot be transferred to seismic drainage durability.

paper_title: Therapeutic Horizons of CRISPR/Cas9 Genome Editing in Overcoming Bacterial Antimicrobial Resistance: A Comprehensive Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Bacterial antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a global public health crisis that threatens to render conventional antibiotic regimens obsolete. The clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats-associated protein 9 (CRISPR/Cas9) system has emerged as a revolutionary tool in molecular biology, offering unmatched sequence-specific genome-editing capabilities. By leveraging custom single-guide RNAs (sgRNAs), CRISPR/Cas9 can precisely target, cleave, or modify specific genomic and plasmid-borne resistance determinants, thereby neutralizing resistance pathways or directly inducing lethal double-strand breaks in pathogenic bacteria. Beyond simple gene disruption, CRISPR-based tools can eliminate resistance-carrying plasmids, block horizontal gene transfer (HGT), impair virulence pathways, and dismantle biofilm architectures while preserving commensal microflora. This narrative review provides a rigorous, updated synthesis of the structural and mechanical framework of CRISPR/Cas9, its targeted application across major multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens, a side-by-side analysis of various delivery systems, and the current balance of therapeutic promise against biological, ecological, and translational safety risks. Furthermore, we outline synergistic integrations with advanced nanocarriers, bacteriophage platforms, synthetic biology, and antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), laying out a prospective roadmap toward publishable clinical translation.

paper_title: Behavioral Organization in Embodied AI: A Three-Level Survey
paper_abstract: Recent years have witnessed a rapid proliferation of learning, control, and planning algorithms for embodied AI. However, grouping methods by model family or learning paradigm often separates approaches serving the same behavioral function, hindering comparison. To address this gap, this survey classifies robotic manipulation research into three functional levels: sensorimotor behavior, reusable units, and task organization. This functional perspective brings together reinforcement learning approaches, vision-language-action models, world models, and code-as-policy methods. The taxonomy supports comparison within functional categories and the transfer of ideas across approaches, offering insights for future algorithm development toward more adaptable embodied systems.

paper_title: Bacteriophage Research in Ecuador Through a One Health Lens: A Scoping Review of Applications, Molecular Characterization, and Translational Evidence
paper_abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Ecuador extends across human health, animal production, agriculture, and the environment, yet national evidence on bacteriophages as an alternative has remained scattered across indexed articles, theses, and institutional repositories. We mapped that evidence through a One Health lens, following the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Five bibliographic databases and publisher platforms (Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Springer, Scopus, and SciELO) and 21 Ecuadorian repositories were searched for studies published between 2021 and 2026. From 592 records, 38 reports met the eligibility criteria: 6 peer-reviewed articles and 32 gray-literature documents (7 postgraduate and 25 undergraduate). Inter-reviewer agreement was 89.1% (Fleiss' kappa = 0.773; 95% CI, 0.635-0.912). Research concentrated in animal health (44.7%) and human health (31.6%), with fewer reports in agriculture (10.5%), poultry (5.3%), aquaculture (5.3%), and the environment (2.6%). Institutional output was highest in Pichincha, Tungurahua, and Guayas; journal articles were affiliated with institutions in Pichincha, Guayas, and Azuay. No included reports were assigned to institutions in the Amazon or Galapagos regions. The most studied hosts were Salmonella enterica, Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Vibrio spp., Listeria spp., and Ralstonia solanacearum. Methodologically, the corpus spans phenotypic characterization, PCR- and restriction-based differentiation, whole-genome sequencing, and functional validation, but these approaches coexist rather than form a maturation gradient. Genomic safety claims rested mainly on the absence of known lysogeny, resistance, and virulence genes, and functional transduction assays were largely absent. Ecuadorian bacteriophage research has begun to shift from demonstrating lysis toward molecularly defined products, but translational readiness is limited by fragmented publication, geographic concentration, and incomplete characterization. Decentralized laboratory capacity, national phage collections with deposited genomes, and standardized characterization pipelines would strengthen the field.

paper_title: Generative AI in Construction Safety: A Systematic Literature Review of Methods, Evidence, Deployment Gaps, and Future Directions
paper_abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly being explored for construction safety; however, its maturity and practical reliability remain unclear. This study systematically reviews GenAI applications in construction safety and assesses whether existing evidence supports reliable, source-grounded, human-supervised, and deployable applications. The review followed a predefined protocol and PRISMA 2020. Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar were searched in May 2026 for studies published from 2019 to August 2026. After duplicate removal and screening, sixty-five studies were included. Data on GenAI methods, safety applications, validation, deployment, and limitations were extracted and synthesized thematically. Six application areas were identified: safety knowledge retrieval and decision support; incident report analysis and risk prediction; multimodal hazard reasoning; synthetic data generation; worker-centered training, communication and behavior support; and generative optimization, monitoring, and safety control. Several studies provided proof-of-concept evidence using historical datasets, simulations, laboratory experiments, or expert assessments, while evidence of generalizability, field deployment, hazard-exposure reduction, and incident prevention remained limited. GenAI showed potential to support hazard recognition, decision support, and compliance-related safety tasks, but field validation, source grounding, and integration with preventive controls are needed for reliable deployment. A conceptual framework linking GenAI capabilities, and preventive safety controls is proposed.

paper_title: CodeHealth Predicts the Token Cost of Agentic Code Review: A Pre-Registered Study of 465 Agent-Authored Pull Requests
paper_abstract: Context: Organizations increasingly delegate code review to multi-agent large language model (LLM) pipelines billed per token. Low code quality raises human maintenance effort, but its effect on agent review cost has not been measured.   Objective: We test whether baseline CodeHealth predicts the token cost of agentic review and fix beyond pull request (PR) footprint.   Method: In a pre-registered observational study, we sampled 465 agent-authored PRs from 246 repositories in AIDev, jointly stratified by CodeHealth and footprint under repository caps. A frozen five-agent review-and-fix pipeline processed every PR with three different LLMs. Per LLM, we fitted a mixed model of log tokens on CodeHealth and log PR footprint, with a repository random intercept.   Results: For all three LLMs the CodeHealth coefficient was negative, with 95% CI excluding zero; each CodeHealth point was associated with 3.5% to 6.1% lower token cost. CodeHealth was unrelated to PR footprint, so PR size does not explain the association. Two of three registered smells predicted fix cost; batch fixing left median CodeHealth unchanged. Exploratory analyses located the association in the review stage, where agents iterated more on unhealthy code without writing more comments. Adjusting for the size of the scored files absorbed the association, which we interpret as mediation by file size.   Conclusions: A quality metric calibrated against human maintainability also predicts the inference cost of multi-agent review and fix. The effect is modest per point and not carried by PR size, so the refactoring case extends to agent-reviewed code when it changes structure and file size, not only the score.   Data Availability: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22127920

paper_title: PremiseCheck: Efficient Fact-Checking of Human and AI Peer Reviews
paper_abstract: Peer review is under strain from the growth of submissions, and review comments written by humans or AI can misstate what a paper says. We introduce ReviewFact, a benchmark that labels such factual errors in review comments under one definition across NLP, machine learning, and the natural sciences, and that measures cost and latency alongside accuracy. A frontier LLM checks comments well but must read the whole paper for each check, while cheap decision models, which score whether a statement holds in a text, fall far short on whole comments that mix several implicit assertions. PremiseCheck is a framework that combines the two. An LLM rewrites each comment as explicit premises without reading the paper, and a decision model checks each premise against the paper. When each comment is checked on its own, PremiseCheck reaches accuracy comparable to GPT-5.5 across all three fields at about half its cost, and on NLP reviews at a quarter of its cost and less than half its latency.

paper_title: ReviewPilot: A Multi-Agent System for Screening and Data Extraction in Systematic Reviews
paper_abstract: Systematic literature reviews follow the PRISMA process of screening scholarly works and extracting evidence from included studies. Deep research tools based on large language models (LLMs) can search and summarize the literature but do not record which studies are excluded or where extracted values come from. We develop a conversational multi-agent system called ReviewPilot that automates the PRISMA workflow from paper screening to information extraction. Researchers can tailor criteria and schemas through dialogue, and a project memory keeps their configurations and revisions. Each screening decision comes with its reason and each extracted value with its source. On epidemiological expert reviews, ReviewPilot outperforms a single-prompt LLM and AgentSLR across three LLMs, with screening macro F1 up to 0.776 and extraction F1 up to 0.788. Case studies in biomedicine and human-computer interaction show close agreement with human annotators, suggesting that ReviewPilot can transfer beyond epidemiology. Code is available at https://github.com/ZhaoqianXue/ReviewPilot.

paper_title: Alignment in Multimodal Large Language Models: A Survey
paper_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can generate fluent responses but may overlook relevant evidence or violate task and safety constraints. This survey examines MLLM alignment through two complementary gaps: the Modality Gap, concerning cross-modal correspondence and the use of task-relevant evidence, and the Intent Gap, concerning behavior relative to specified goals, constraints, and human expectations. We organize the literature along six dimensions: architecture, objective functions, data construction, training, evaluation, and applications. Across these dimensions, we link alignment mechanisms and supervision assumptions to the failures they target and the evidence supporting their effectiveness. Our analysis clarifies what interface compatibility, target imitation, preference learning, and verifiable rewards can each demonstrate about alignment, together with the limitations of their underlying supervision. We further summarize evaluation at the representation, task, and behavior levels, emphasizing evidence dependence, constraint compliance, and the distinction between observed improvements and explanations of their underlying mechanisms. Applications in robotics, safety, healthcare, recommendation, and climate decision support reveal three recurring requirements: traceable evidence, valid supervision, and decisions that respect domain constraints. Building on this synthesis, we identify four research directions: evidence-consistent alignment across modalities, verified self-correction and test-time alignment, diagnosis-guided repair, and reliable transfer to underrepresented settings.

paper_title: A Survey of Security in Real-World Agents: From Digital Agents to Embodied AI
paper_abstract: Real-world agents extend language-model reasoning to digital operations and physical action, raising a central security question: how do digital-side attacks cross trust boundaries in robotic systems, and what physical safety conclusions can existing evidence support? This survey examines semantic hijacking, sensory manipulation, and middleware injection across software agents, modular robotic agents, and vision-language-action (VLA) systems. We compare how untrusted content acquires task authority, corrupted observations affect action generation, and middleware access reaches execution interfaces under different permission and control assumptions. An experiment-level analysis examines environment, trajectory, privilege and exposure, consequence, and assurance, distinguishing generated plans, software-state changes, simulated execution, and physical robot actions. The comparison reveals important evidence boundaries: RoboPAIR evaluates driving plans in Dolphins but API-mediated robot actions in Jackal, while Apollo point-cloud replay demonstrates altered braking decisions without measuring physical deceleration. These differences prevent planning or command-level success from being treated as direct evidence of physical safety violations. Across defenses, protection depends on the integrity of the state used for checking, coverage of executable command paths, and the timing of intervention. Reported attack suppression also need not imply useful protection: Safe Prompting reduces targeted attack success to zero while clean-task success also falls to zero in its LIBERO evaluation. Together, these findings identify the conditions under which digital compromise reaches physical execution, delimit the safety claims supported by current experiments, and motivate stronger assurance of action enforcement and recovery under compromised state.

paper_title: A Survey of Automatic Humor Detection: From Theoretical Foundations to Large Language Models
paper_abstract: Automatic humor detection, the computational task of identifying humorous content, is increasingly critical as Large Language Models (LLMs) integrate into communication platforms such as chatbots and virtual assistants. However, humor poses challenges for AI due to its reliance on context, cultural nuances, linguistic ambiguity, and multimodal cues. Current research is fragmented across humor types, languages, modalities, and evaluation benchmarks, particularly regarding modern LLM capabilities and limitations. This survey synthesizes the automatic humor detection field, tracing its evolution from foundational psychological and linguistic theories through classical machine learning, deep learning, and transformer-based LLMs. We organize and analyze computational methods, feature engineering techniques, benchmark datasets (text-only, multimodal, multilingual), and evaluation metrics. We examine LLM adaptation strategies, including fine-tuning, parameter-efficient methods (PEFT), prompt engineering, and multi-task learning, alongside multimodal and cross-lingual humor understanding developments. Our analysis reveals that while LLMs show improved performance in capturing surface humor patterns, gaps persist in pragmatic reasoning, cultural grounding, multimodal integration, and explainability. We identify open challenges, including data scarcity, evaluation inconsistencies, the humor–offensiveness boundary, and the need for culturally aware and interpretable models. By consolidating progress and pinpointing limitations, this survey guides future interdisciplinary research toward developing socially intelligent AI systems capable of understanding humor.

paper_title: Industry 4.0, Quality and Industry 4.0. Implementation in Slovakia: A Longitudinal Analysis Based on the Industry 4UM Survey (2017–2025)
paper_abstract: Industry 4.0 has become a key driver of industrial digital transformation, enabling enterprises to improve productivity, flexibility, and competitiveness through the integration of advanced digital technologies. Although the strategic importance of Industry 4.0 is widely recognized, the pace and maturity of its implementation vary considerably across enterprises and regions. This study presents a longitudinal evaluation of Industry 4.0 adoption in the Slovak Republic based on annual Industry4UM survey data collected between 2017 and 2025. The analysis focuses on three indicators: the size distribution of participating enterprises, the implementation phase of Industry 4.0, and the perceived importance of Industry 4.0 for future business development. The results indicate that the survey maintained participation from enterprises of different sizes throughout the observation period, providing a broad representation of the Slovak industrial environment. The implementation analysis revealed a gradual increase in the proportion of enterprises reaching the adaptation phase, accompanied by a substantial decline in the number of organizations that had not yet initiated Industry 4.0 activities. At the same time, respondents consistently expressed a highly positive perception of Industry 4.0, while negative attitudes remained negligible. A comparison of enterprise perception and implementation demonstrates that awareness of Industry 4.0 has advanced more rapidly than practical adoption, indicating that the principal challenge is no longer recognizing the importance of digital transformation but facilitating its effective implementation. The findings provide a comprehensive overview of the evolution of Industry 4.0 adoption in Slovak industry and offer insights that may support policymakers, researchers, and industrial practitioners in designing future digital transformation strategies. In this article, we also examine the State of Israel’s approach to Industry 4.0 from several perspectives. We focus on how both the Israeli industrial sector and government agencies support and implement Industry 4.0. Israeli government agencies, businesses, and institutions also focus on social and economic issues and on structural changes in the labour market related to Industry 4.0.

paper_title: Beyond the Symptom Score: What Standard Psychiatric Rating Scales Fail to Capture — A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Standard psychiatric rating scales such as the PANSS, HAM-D and MADRS remain the dominant outcome measures in clinical trials and routine care, yet they were built to quantify symptom severity rather than to register the full range of change that matters to patients. This narrative review synthesized psychometric, validation, epidemiological and trial evidence, together with consensus reports, to identify clinically and personally meaningful improvements that symptom-focused scales fail to detect. Evidence converged on ten under-measured outcome domains: real-world functioning, which correlates only weakly with symptoms and often lags behind them; cognition and social cognition; negative symptoms and motivational anhedonia; the subjective experience of medication; quality of life and positive mental health; personal recovery (connectedness, hope, identity, meaning and empowerment); internalized stigma; physical health and premature mortality, with all-cause mortality two to three-and-a-half times that of the general population; sleep and circadian function; and shared decision-making as a process outcome of care. Two cross-cutting limitations compound these gaps: systematic discordance among clinician, self-report and informant ratings, and the inability of retrospective, clinic-based instruments to capture the momentary, context-dependent dynamics now accessible through ecological momentary assessment and passive sensing. We propose a pragmatic, tiered outcome set that pairs every symptom scale with measures of functioning and of quality of life or recovery, adds physical health, sleep and medication burden, and reserves digital methods for settings that can support them. Improvement in psychiatry is multidimensional; measuring it as such is a scientific necessity, not a refinement.

paper_title: Cancer Information Burden and Mental Health Among U.S. Cancer Caregivers: Evidence from the Health Information National Trends Survey
paper_abstract: Background: Family and unpaid caregivers play an essential role in supporting individuals with cancer and frequently navigate complex health information related to treatment, symptoms, supportive care, and healthcare services. Difficulty obtaining, understanding, and evaluating cancer information may contribute to psychological distress among caregivers. However, nationally representative evidence examining the association between cancer information burden and caregiver psychological well-being remains limited. Objective: This study examined the association between cancer information burden and psychological distress among U.S. adults who reported providing care to an individual with cancer. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of pooled data from the National Cancer Institute’s Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS) Cycles 6 and 7. Cancer caregivers were identified based on respondents reporting caregiving for an individual with cancer. Cancer information burden was measured using four items assessing the effort required to obtain cancer information, difficulty understanding cancer information, frustration during cancer information seeking, and concern about information quality. Item responses were averaged to create a composite cancer information burden score, with higher scores indicating greater burden. Psychological distress was measured using the Patient Health Questionnaire-4 (PHQ-4), a validated 4-item measure of depressive and anxiety symptoms ranging from 0 to 12. Survey-weighted linear regression examined the association between cancer information burden and PHQ-4 scores while accounting for the complex survey design. Adjusted models included age, sex, race and ethnicity, education, and household income. Results: We identified 241 respondents as cancer caregivers, with 124 included in the fully adjusted complete-case analysis. In the common analytic sample, higher cancer information burden was associated with greater psychological distress in unadjusted analysis (β=1.57, 95% CI 0.17-2.98; p=.028). After adjustment for age, sex, race and ethnicity, education, and household income, the association remained statistically significant (β=0.89, 95% CI 0.03-1.75; p=.042). Older age was associated with lower psychological distress in the fully adjusted model (β=-0.06, 95% CI -0.11 to -0.01; p=.013). Several education and income categories were also associated with psychological distress. Diagnostic analyses supported an approximately linear relationship between information burden and PHQ-4 scores, although heteroskedasticity was present. Conclusions: Greater cancer information burden was associated with higher psychological distress among U.S. cancer caregivers. These findings suggest that caregiver well-being may be influenced not only by access to cancer information but also by the effort, complexity, frustration, and uncertainty involved in navigating that information. Interventions and digital health resources designed for cancer caregivers should therefore consider strategies to reduce information burden and improve caregivers' ability to identify, understand, and evaluate cancer-related information.

paper_title: Can Patients Be Highly Satisfied Despite Little Clinical Improvement—or Dissatisfied Despite Substantial Improvement? A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Patient satisfaction has become a dominant metric of health care quality, embedded in public reporting, accreditation, and pay-for-performance programs. Its prominence rests on an implicit assumption that satisfied patients have been treated well and have improved. This narrative review synthesizes conceptual and empirical literature to examine whether, how often, and why patients can be highly satisfied despite minimal clinical gain or dissatisfied despite substantial gain. The 2 constructs are related but explain little of each other. In a cohort of 2116 surgical patients, no outcome measure accounted for more than 8% of the variance in satisfaction, which tracked absolute postoperative state rather than change. Complications and readmissions show weak, inconsistent associations with satisfaction, whereas communication and shared decision-making are strongly and independently associated with it. Six mechanisms explain the divergence: expectancy disconfirmation (unmet expectations raised the odds of dissatisfaction after knee arthroplasty more than 10-fold), relational determinants, health-status confounding, placebo and nocebo effects, response shift (detected in 86.7% of longitudinal studies), and measurement artifacts such as ceiling effects and response bias. In low- and middle-income settings, more than half of respondents rated poor-quality care as good or better. Satisfaction should be neither discarded nor used as a surrogate for effectiveness; complementary measurement of care experience, clinical outcome, and expectation fulfillment is the defensible path.

paper_title: Artificial Intelligence and Engagement Pricing in Accounting Firms: A Literature Review and Research Agenda
paper_abstract: Accounting firms are adopting artificial intelligence (AI) quickly, but the way they plan and price engagements has changed much more slowly. This paper reviews research from four areas that rarely meet: the pricing of accounting and audit services, the productivity effects of AI on knowledge work, the use of AI in accounting and auditing, and activity-based costing and project control. The review finds that AI's effects on accounting work are large but uneven across tasks, that new review and oversight work appears alongside time savings, and that hours freed by AI are often absorbed by other work rather than appearing as lower recorded effort. Firm-level studies link AI investment to lower audit fees and to changes in staff mix, but almost no research examines how firms adjust the internal, hours-based plans on which fees are set. I identify six gaps: the measurement of activity-level AI effects, the cost of oversight, the fate of freed capacity, in-engagement monitoring, the sharing of AI gains with clients, and the position of small and mid-sized practices. I then propose a research agenda of seven questions with suggested methods and data. The paper aims to help researchers and practitioners study and manage AI-enabled engagements on the basis of evidence rather than general efficiency assumptions.

paper_title: Responsible and Trustworthy Agentic AI: Governance, Assurance, Explainability, Controllability, and Human Oversight: A Comprehensive Survey
paper_abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence combines goal-directed reasoning, planning, memory, tool use, adaptation and multi-agent coordination with the ability to affect external systems. This capability raises problems of authorization, safety, human oversight, accountability and the evidence required to justify reliance. This non-systematic integrative survey distinguishes AI ethics, responsible AI, governance, trustworthiness, assurance, explainability, security and controllability; synthesizes preventive, detective, corrective, human-based and agent-based controls; and compares responsibility and oversight arrangements across the agent lifecycle. Building on established governance and meaningful-human-control research, it proposes an authority-control-assurance-accountability mapping that connects normative requirements to delegated decision rights, enforceable controls, observable evidence, escalation conditions and identifiable organizational owners. Two fictional cases illustrate the proposed mapping for document access and software changes. The framework is a conceptual synthesis rather than an empirically validated assurance standard. The survey identifies limitations of supervisory-agent independence, long-horizon explanation, dynamic authorization and continuous re-assurance, and specifies research questions for future evaluation.

paper_title: Academic Integrity in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Scoping Review (2026)
paper_abstract: The rapid proliferation of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and large language models (LLMs) has fundamentally transformed the landscape of modern higher education, prompting a critical paradigm shift in how academic integrity is conceptualized. This scoping review synthesizes 20 cutting-edge academic publications from 2026 (retrieved via Google Scholar) to examine the evolution of academic integrity from mechanical plagiarism detection and punitive surveillance toward comprehensive institutional, pedagogical, and ethical redesign. The synthesis reveals that the primary systemic catalyst for academic misconduct remains the pervasive “publish or perish” culture and quantitative assessment paradigms that prioritize performance over moral growth. Contemporary scholarship moves beyond identifying individual infractions to address systemic vulnerabilities, student uncertainty, data privacy, and the degradation of higher-order cognitive skills (analyzing, evaluating, creating) resulting from unreflective AI reliance.
